Additionally, CENTCOM that U.S. Marines boarded the tanker M/T Wen Yao in the Gulf of Oman as part of Washington's renewed naval blockade of Iran, which it claims had redirected three commercial vessels and disabled one that refused to comply. Iranian Health Ministry spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour on X that renewed U.S. airstrikes have killed at least 38 people and wounded more than 400 so far in July. Iran widens its retaliatory attacks: Iran launched attacks on U.S. military installations in the Gulf, hitting targets in Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, and Bahrain. It also widened its range of targets, hitting locations in Jordan, Syria, and Iraq. Iran Arash attack drones at the Isa Air Base in Bahrain, its army reported, targeting U.S. helicopters and reconnaissance aircraft. Iran a base in Kuwait, claiming to have targeted its defensive radar capacities, weapons depot, HIMARS launchers, and missile stockpile. Kuwait Friday one of its power generation and water desalination plants was hit in what it called a "sinful Iranian attack," sparking a fire and damaging the facility and several electricity generation units. Iranian missiles Qatar, with debris from one attack injuring a child, according to the country's Interior Ministry. The country's Defense Ministry reported multiple missile interceptions on Thursday and Friday, and condemned Iran for its "sinful aggression." Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed to have destroyed a "long-range radar system" and several military targets in an attack on the U.S. Al-Udeid Air Base in Qatar. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard also that it carried out a "surprise attack" on a U.S.-led coalition special operations center in Al-Tanf, southern Syria. The U.S. announced that it had left Al-Tanf in February, and it is not clear whether any U.S. personnel were at the facility at the time of the attack. The Iranian navy early on Friday that it had targeted a maritime-control radar installation on Oman's As Salamah islands and air-control radar in Oman's Ghanam region. Iraqi authorities said five drones struck the city of Erbil on Thursday, adding that two of these crashed and one was shot down. Satellite imagery published by an open-source intelligence account that an Iranian Shahed drone hit a U.S. Patriot missile launcher in the city, though no official confirmation has been issued and Iran's military had not claimed responsibility for the attack. Satellite imagery on Thursday by the mapping firm Soar appeared to contradict earlier claims by the UAE that a fire at the Zayed Military City was on July 13 "accidental," potentially adding to the list of confirmed Iranian strikes over the course of the last week. Iran 's ambassador condemns U.S. attacks on civilian infrastructure as "war crimes": Amir Saeid Iravani, Iran's UN ambassador, U.S. attacks on Iranian civilian infrastructure as "acts of aggression" and "war crimes" in a letter to the UN Secretary-General and the Security Council, accusing Washington of deliberately and illegally striking civilian targets. Oil market burning through its emergency stocks, threatening wider shock: Fatih Birol, the chief of the United States Energy Information Agency, warned Bloomberg about the danger of rising energy prices, telling the outlet the danger is "not months. It is weeks." IEA chief Fatih Birol that the U.S.'s historic 400-million-barrel emergency release helped push barrel prices down by $20. Birol also told Bloomberg that higher petroleum production from the U.S., Brazil, and Kazakhstan had also limited the shock, as did draws from the U.S.'s reserves, and Saudi and Emirati efforts to bypass Hormuz. But, he warned, none of these reprieves were "endless." The U.S. EIA has reported crude stocks at Oklahoma's Cushing facility fell below 20 million barrels in June and may continue to be near "tank bottoms," the minimum oil that must remain in tanks and pipelines for pumps to work. The analytics firm Kpler separately on Thursday that oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz had fallen by 62% to 4.1 million barrels a day, claiming that a full shutdown had been prevented by the use of alternate export routes and softer Chinese demand for petroleum, roughly corresponding to a similar report by Goldman Sachs analysts. The firm reported only eight crossings through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, seven of which used the northern Iranian corridor. Vance responds to Drop Site 's reporting: Vice President** JD Vance a Thursday report from Drop Site's Jeremy Scahill and Ryan Grim, in which a senior Iranian official said that Tehran sent Vance a private message warning that Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were exploiting their access to U.S.-Iran negotiations for financial gain. "This is completely bogus. I never received a message like this," Vance wrote, calling the allegation that they traded on insider information "absurd," adding that "no one has done more" than Kushner and Witkoff "to work towards peace and prosperity" in the Middle East. Drop Site's full report on Iran's warning about Witkoff and Kushner is available . Lebanon Israel continues violating Lebanon ceasefire with overnight attacks: Israeli forces raiding the town of Haris in the Tyre (Sour) district, several civilians in an overnight attack, according to Lebanon's National News Agency, prompting these civilians to appeal to the Lebanese Army for evacuation. Also in Tyre, an Israeli drone the Mansouri area and the Naqoura road, wounding a Syrian national. Israeli artillery also the towns of Baraachit and Hadatha in the Bint Jbeil district, where Israeli forces carried out a large-scale demolition. Palestine Israel kills 14 Palestinians in attacks on Gaza: Israel 14 Palestinians and wounded at least 37 in separate attacks in Gaza on Friday, Al Jazeera reported. At least eight Palestinians were killed and 20 others wounded after an Israeli drone struck a group of Palestinians in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, according to Gaza-based Safa News Agency. The strike targeted the gathering as the funeral procession of a Palestinian who had been killed earlier passed through the area. Israel struck an apartment building in Gaza City, killing one and wounding others. In northern Gaza, an Israeli drone strike in Beit Lahia killed a 52-year-old woman. One person was also killed and three others injured after an Israeli strike hit a makeshift shelter housing displaced people, west of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza. Israel pushes its "Yellow Line" to Gaza's main north-south artery: Israeli forces Gaza City's Zeitoun neighborhood under heavy gunfire, killing one Palestinian, wounding three others, destroying homes and shops, and forcing families to flee, according to reporting from Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed. By morning, they had pushed the "yellow line," the boundary marking the edge of Israeli military control, in violation of the October 2025 agreement, to Salah al-Din Road--the 45-kilometer artery connecting northern and southern Gaza and passing through every governorate. A witness described quadcopters and shelling surrounding displaced families overnight, forcing women to sleep in the street. "We don't know where to flee to," he said. Separately, on Thursday, senior military officials reportedly Israel's Security Cabinet that Israel now controls between 67% and 70% of the Gaza Strip, according to the Jerusalem Post. Israeli attacks in Gaza at highest level since October "ceasefire," conflict monitor reports: Israeli attacks on Gaza their highest level since the October 2025 agreement, according to the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED) via Reuters. ACLED recorded more than 40 Israeli air and drone strikes in June--the highest monthly total since the truce. Israeli guards beat Palestinian physician and denied him medical care: Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya his lawyers on July 14 that Israeli prison guards beat him again following a previous legal visit on July 2, adding that he remains in solitary confinement in an underground prison and has been denied medical care for an injury to his right eye, according to Physicians for Human Rights Israel. "Do everything possible to get me out of this place," Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya told his lawyers, noting the discontinuation of his pain medication and a refusal to give him the results of a recently conducted X-ray. During the visit, Abu Safiya was concealed from his lawyers behind an opaque partition and forced to communicate by telephone while masked prison guards remained close enough to hear the conversation. Abu Safiya, the former director of Kamal Adwan Hospital, has been imprisoned without charge or trial since December 2024 after refusing to abandon his patients. Gaza flotilla participant files rape complaint against Israeli prison guards: Anna Liedtke, a 25-year-old activist aboard the Gaza-bound aid Freedom Flotilla, a criminal complaint in Israel accusing female guards at Givon Prison of raping her during a forced strip search, according to The Guardian. Liedtke alleges guards forced her to her knees, restrained her and covered her mouth to stop her screams, while male guards watched and laughed. Israeli forces detained Liedtke after seizing her Gaza-bound aid ship in international waters on October 8, 2025, and held her for five days. Liedtke said the abuse was intended to intimidate activists into abandoning solidarity with Palestinians, adding that her assault was "way, way less than what Palestinian prisoners experience." More than a dozen other flotilla activists have also reported sexual assault. In May, Drop Site published Liedtke's first-person account, co-authored with journalist Noa Avishag Schnall, detailing their abduction and abuse. Read. Channel 14 report shows Israeli officials praising Gaza 's destruction and displacement of Palestinians: A new report by Israel's Channel 14 senior Israeli government and military officials openly celebrating the destruction of large parts of Gaza and the mass killing and displacement of Palestinians. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said he felt "good" seeing neighborhoods such as Jabaliya and Shuja'iyya "destroyed" and "in ruins," describing the devastation as the result of a deliberate policy. He added that Israeli forces would not withdraw from the so-called "yellow line" unless Hamas disarms, saying: "And even after that, we will remain in Gaza!" Deputy Israeli military chief Maj. Gen. Tamir Yadai described the situation as a "victory," citing Israel's control of 65% of Gaza, claiming that "70,000 terrorists" had been killed. Al Jazeera: Undercover investigation exposes UK and Canadian funding of illegal Israeli settlements: An undercover investigation by Al-Jazeera says it has uncovered evidence that charities and donors in the United Kingdom and Canada are helping channel tax-deductible donations to Israeli settler organizations in the occupied West Bank, despite laws prohibiting charitable funds from supporting illegal settlements. Posing as prospective donors, Al Jazeera's undercover reporters were allegedly told by pro-settler organisations that donations could be routed through registered charities before being used to expand settlements, campaign for the demolition of Palestinian homes, and provide military-grade equipment, including drones, to settlers. Watch the full investigation by Al Jazeera . U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Marco Rubio launches major push against "far-left terrorists," says new designations are coming soon: Speaking at a conference attended by officials from more than 60 countries, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the U.S. is building an "international counterterrorism coalition" focused on transnational far-left networks, alleging links to Iranian proxies and Cuba. Rubio promised further terrorist designations and coordinated intelligence, law enforcement, and financial action. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the government is examining nonprofits and charities for alleged illicit financing, foreign influence, and tax-exempt abuse, while claiming a "new operational alliance" between "international Marxism and radical Islamic movements." Homeland Security Adviser Stephen Miller said NSPM-7 would be used to debank, defund, and disrupt left-wing groups, dismissing civil-liberties objections and calling them "enemies of civilization." The State Department a new visa restriction policy targeting foreign nationals it says support or enable "far-left terrorist" and aligned groups, including through incitement, financing, recruitment, logistical support, criminal activity, or economic sabotage. It also released new visa rules for foreign students, journalists, and cultural exchange visitors. Student and cultural exchange visas would be limited to four years. Visas for foreign journalists will be cut down from five years to 240 days, and just 90 days for Chinese journalists. Trump uses televised address to allege Chinese interference in 2020 election: In a primetime on Thursday evening, President Trump made a series of unsubstantiated claims about the 2020 election and claimed he was "declassifying" additional documents that would corroborate what he called "shocking vulnerabilities in our election infrastructure." Several networks, including ABC and NBC, refused to carry the speech (but streamed it online), which Trump criticized during his remarks, calling it "part of a plot." He also addressed the war in Iran, saying that the U.S. was "winning big" and promising his audience that they would "see the fruits of that labor very, very shortly." ICE agent who killed man in Maine accused of violent, troubled past: The ICE agent who shot and 26-year-old Johan Sebasti an Duran Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine, on Monday has been identified as David Michael Brouillette , 37, a former Maine law enforcement officer and Army veteran, the Portland Press Herald reported. His ex-wife, Ashley Brouillette , said he called her and admitted to the shooting and asked her to "lie for him." Ashley Brouillette also alleged that her ex-husband was abusive during their relationship and that she had previously reported concerns about his mental health to his military superiors. DHS has refused to confirm his identity. Rep. Ilhan Omar pushes U.S. to join ICC: Rep.Ilhan Omar a resolution on Thursday urging the United States to join the International Criminal Court, The Guardian reports, marking the first congressional pushback against Rubio 's pledge to "systematically disable" the war crimes tribunal. "The ICC is a crucial tool for justice in places where victims have nowhere else to turn," Omar said. "No one is above the law." The resolution comes after the Trump administration imposed waves of sanctions on the court and its officials over its investigations into Israeli war crimes in Gaza and the West Bank. 125 countries recognize the ICC. Court-appointed UAW monitor pressures Fain over Gaza: The Detroit News reported on Thursday that Neil Barofsky , the court-appointed monitor overseeing the United Auto Workers, had bullied UAW President Shawn Fain over the union's call for a Gaza ceasefire in 2023. Drop Site obtained and authenticated a recording of this conversation, which contradicts several claims Barofsky made about the call's contents. In the December 2023 phone call, Neil Barofsky told Fain that his statement invoking the union's history against fascism and apartheid "potentially cross[ed] the line into the area of antisemitism" by drawing a parallel to Israel's conduct. Fain, now under a federal grand jury investigation over allegations of corruption and retaliation following a highly critical report issued by the union's federal monitor, has described Barofsky's conduct as driven by a "personal vendetta" stemming from a "political grudge" Barofsky holds. Rep. Rashida Tlaib, who represents a district covering much of the Detroit area, has called on Barofsky to resign. A full transcript of the call and more about the dispute is available in the latest from Ryan Grim for Drop Site. Trump Media to charge for quicker access to Truth Social posts: Trump Media & Technology Group "Truth API," a licensed data feed set to launch August 1 that will give banks and trading firms "the fastest access" to posts from the platform's 10 most influential accounts, including President Donald Trump's, the company announced on Thursday. The product is reportedly being marketed towards algorithmic trading firms and was designed, according to its interim CEO, to provide the company with a new revenue stream. Trump has made several announcements on Truth Social that have dramatically moved the markets, including announcements about the ongoing war against Iran and the announcement of tariffs on "Liberation Day." White House teleprompter operator probed for insider betting on speeches : Gabriel Perez , President Trump's teleprompter operator since 2016, is in with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to settle allegations that he used inside knowledge of Trump's speeches to win more than $100,000 betting on the prediction market Kalshi, ABC News reported on Thursday. Trump placed Perez on unpaid administrative leave after Kalshi flagged the suspicious trading activity to regulators, according to White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt. War official could profit heavily from suit against the Pentagon: Deputy Secretary of War Stephen Feinberg , who helped found the private-equity giant Cerberus, could stand to benefit tremendously from a lawsuit filed by the satellite firm Ligado Networks, which is a major recipient of Cerberus backing, against the Pentagon, according to a new investigation from The American Prospect. Ligado Networks is suing the Department of War for $40 billion over a satellite spectrum dispute, one of the largest in American history. Feinberg's Cerberus holdings are in trusts controlled by his children, Sen. Elizabeth Warren has pointed out, and, in a 2026 ethics statement, Feinberg said he would continue contracting with the firm he helped found for "administrative services." Read the full article from The American Prospect . Other International News Ansarallah promises to block Saudi access to Bab al-Mandab in retaliation for airport attack: Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a high-ranking official in Yemen's Ansarallah, told Drop Site News that the group will block Saudi access to the Bab al-Mandab strait, the chokepoint linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, in retaliation for Monday's strikes on Sana'a airport. Al-Bukhaiti called the strait a "legitimate leverage tool" and promised a "blockade-for-blockade" arrangement, targeting only countries "participating in the aggression against Yemen." The leader of the Houthi movement, Abdulmalek al-Houthi, went further on Thursday, declaring "all Saudi oil facilities and vital installations" targets. Read the Drop Site exclusive from contributor Iona Craig. Armed assailants seize chemical tanker off Yemen coast: Armed assailants of the chemical tanker Asana off Yemen's southern coast in the Gulf of Aden on Friday, in an incident maritime security sources believe is linked to Somali piracy rather than Yemen's Houthi militia, Reuters reported. The vessel issued a distress call around 10 a.m. local time and had no armed security team aboard, according to British maritime security group Ambrey. The circumstances of the takeover and the current status of the crew and the vessel were unclear as of Friday morning. The EU's Aspides naval mission has been tasked with assisting in recovery efforts, and a South Korean warship remains in the area. Nigeria completes evacuation of 1,490 citizens from South Africa : Nigeria's foreign ministry Thursday it has completed the voluntary evacuation of 1,490 citizens from South Africa following xenophobic attacks, according to Reuters. The Nigerian government said the evacuations followed talks with South African authorities over security concerns, including the deaths of at least two Nigerian nationals allegedly assaulted by security officials. Russian attacks on Ukraine kill 4: Russian attacks on Ukraine overnight killed four people and wounded others, the Associated Press , with two killed in a strike on Odesa and 10 wounded and two others killed in Zaporizhzhia, where five additional people were injured. One of the people killed in Odesa was a woman walking her children, Ukrainian officials said, noting that her children survived the attack. Three civilians were killed and seven were injured in Russian-occupied Kherson, Russian authorities relayed. The strikes come amid a major shakeup in Ukraine's leadership: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced his intention to replace Mykhailo Fedorov as the country's defense minister with Yevhen Khmara, the head of Ukraine's security services. Fedorov's ouster sparked protests in Kyiv on Thursday. Sudan 's army says it destroyed over 200 RSF vehicles in two-week offensive: The Sudanese army on Thursday that it destroyed about 205 combat vehicles, 17 supply trucks and four Rapid Support Forces drones between July 1 and July 15, with the heaviest losses reported in North Kordofan and Darfur, according to Sudan Tribune. The military also said it recaptured the Blue Nile town of Kurmuk after intense fighting and pledged that operations would continue across all fronts "until security and stability are restored." U.S. approves nearly $2 billion weapons sale to Saudi Arabia : The State Department a potential $1.96 billion weapons sale to Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, including up to 20,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon Systems, aimed at bolstering the kingdom's air defenses as the U.S.-Israel war on Iran re-escalates, Al Jazeera . The sale, with BAE Systems as principal contractor, comes as Saudi Arabia faces potential renewed conflict with Yemen's Houthis, who threatened to target Saudi oil facilities if Riyadh joins what they called "comprehensive aggression" against Yemen. China condemns UK nationalization of British Steel : China's Ministry of Commerce Friday that the UK's nationalization of British Steel, formalized Thursday, "severely undermined" Chinese companies' confidence in investing in Britain, calling the move a "forcible" takeover that disregarded former owner Jingye's contributions. Jingye, one of China's biggest companies, bought British Steel for $94 million in 2020 and, by 2025, reported daily losses of $942,000 on the company. The British government began its nationalization in response to concerns that Jingye would begin shutting down British Steel's Scunthorpe Blast furnaces, and has promised to appoint an independent valuer to "assess whether any compensation is payable" to Jingye. Kim Jong Un meets senior Chinese official, pledges deeper ties: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un Thursday with Wang Huning, China's fourth-highest-ranked official, and pledged to deepen ties with Beijing, state-run KCNA reported. Following the visit, Wang said that China's "firm support for the cause of Korean socialism led by Comrade General Secretary Kim Jong Un will never be changed." The summit follows Chinese President Xi Jinping's June visit to Pyongyang, his first in seven years, and is seen as an effort by Beijing to reinforce its influence over North Korea. That work taught me how to follow the paper trail, ask uncomfortable questions, and hold people accountable. I joined the Auditor General’s office for the same reason: to make sure our seniors and kids weren’t getting shortchanged by backroom deals. In 2019, everything changed. Our mayor resigned after pleading guilty to extortion. I couldn’t stand by and raise my family in a place where the establishment tolerates this kind of government corruption. So I ran as an Independent against the local machine and won. It was one of the proudest and toughest things I have ever done. As mayor, I refused a city car and gas card, cut costs, and insisted on accountability. We eliminated cash payments, turned a deficit into a surplus, and improved the city’s credit rating. I secured over $155 million in state and federal grants to fix streets, tackle blight, and rebuild neighborhoods. **Why am I telling you this? Because I’m running for Congress for the same simple reason I ran for mayor: to make government work for you. clean_body: Please read | = = Peter, it’s Paige Cognetti, and I have a message for you. I didn’t set out to be a politician. I joined the Scranton School Board because I believe in the simple idea that government should work as hard as the people it serves. That work taught me how to follow the paper trail, ask uncomfortable questions, and hold people accountable. I joined the Auditor General’s office for the same reason: to make sure our seniors and kids weren’t getting shortchanged by backroom deals. In 2019, everything changed. Our mayor resigned after pleading guilty to extortion. I couldn’t stand by and raise my family in a place where the establishment tolerates this kind of government corruption. So I ran as an Independent against the local machine and won. It was one of the proudest and toughest things I have ever done. As mayor, I refused a city car and gas card, cut costs, and insisted on accountability. We eliminated cash payments, turned a deficit into a surplus, and improved the city’s credit rating. Because I’m running for Congress for the same simple reason I ran for mayor: to make government work for you. I traveled with three of my House colleagues to Havana, Cuba, to witness for ourselves how the Trump administration’s cruel blockade is crushing the Cuban people.
This administration is cruelly blockading resources, including fuel, into Cuba and is weaponizing international tariffs against any country that tries to assist Cuba in this time of extreme need. They have intentionally created a humanitarian crisis.
All of this, without ANY evidence that Cuba is a threat to our national security.
The Trump administration has blocked nearly all fuel deliveries since January. This has resulted in nationwide blackouts for days, food and healthcare shortages, school closures, and has made it nearly impossible to have any business open at all. That means basic services and essential facilities, like hospitals, are running on next to nothing.
This week, the White House unveiled MORE sanctions without any attempt to negotiate a solution that promotes respect for human rights. This administration is not only putting innocent Cuban civilians at risk, but they are also imperiling American servicemembers.
As a critical care physician in the House, I will do all that I can to remove the foreign policy obstacles preventing the Cuban people from having safety, security, and access to healthcare. And I need your help to do it.
Will you support our movement to flip the House and Senate this November, and ultimately, impeach the felon-in-chief? We need all the support we can to stop Trump from using American tax dollars to wage cruel and illegal sieges against other countries. clean_body: Working families can't afford this manufactured crisis. Citizenship is the solution. | | | Peter, All of us rely on workers to keep this country running — including immigrants, who make up nearly one in three direct care workers in nursing homes, assisted living centers, and home health care — the people caring for our parents, grandparents, and disabled loved ones.1 As daily life gets more expensive for working families, the federal government is making our conditions worse: pushing millions of working people out of status, out of work, and out of the families and communities that depend on them. Already, tens of thousands of TPS holders are at risk of being laid off following last month’s Supreme Court decision.2 In-home care now costs families more than $80,000 a year — and experts warn that deepening worker shortages will drive costs even higher.1 As this administration strips protections from millions, escalates deadly enforcement across the country, and pushes workers out of the labor force, we need real solutions that protect the safety of everyone in our communities and create stability, not chaos, for all of us. Citizenship is the best solution to stop the chaos and instability that mass delegalization is forcing onto working families, employers, local economies, and entire industries. That's why Congress must deliver citizenship — because our families, our caregivers, and our communities need stability, not manufactured crisis. # [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
The numbers are in, Peter.
Greg Abbott’s newest campaign finance filing is officially public, and it’s as clear as day who Abbott is _really_ working for.
The hard numbers prove that Abbott’s campaign is completely bankrolled by a group of billionaires and corporate interests. Meanwhile, our campaign is powered by everyday Texans who believe this state belongs to us, not billionaires.
**Nearly 4 out of every 5 dollars Abbott raised came from just 79 six-figure donor records.** Just 100 ultra-wealthy donors accounted for 83.7% of his entire multi-million dollar haul.
On the other hand, more than **_74,000 individual donors_** have pitched in to power Gina’s campaign. Our average gift was just **$13** , and 97.5% of our contributions are $100 or less — coming from right here in Texas.

Peter,

One of the questions I get asked most often is what I enjoyed most about serving in the Iowa legislature. People are usually surprised by my answer.

I loved the work that happened behind the scenes. I loved digging into the research, reading the law, and figuring out how to solve complicated problems. I was one of the few legislators who wrote my own bills because I wanted to understand every word that went into them.

But if I'm being honest, that wasn't my favorite part of the job. **The part I loved most was serving my constituents.**

There is nothing quite like getting a call from someone who's been stuck in a bureaucratic maze and helping them cut through red tape. Sometimes it's helping a family access benefits they've earned. Sometimes it's resolving an issue that's been hanging over someone's head for weeks. Sometimes it's just pointing someone in the right direction.

Those moments don't make the news, but they're what public service is really about. That's what I'm looking forward to most in Congress. I can't thank you enough for all your support to help me get there.

Month after month, you continue to show up, and every time you do, I'm humbled. **Knowing there are so many people who believe in this campaign and the kind of leadership we're fighting for gives me so much hope. Thanks to you, in fact, we just reached our $10,000 mid-month goal!**

We still have a long road ahead, but I couldn't ask for better people to be walking it with me.

Thank you,

Christina

---
Friend, America is gripped by a severe, crushing housing crisis. **Right now in Connecticut, half of all renters and a quarter of all homeowners are cost-burdened – meaning they are forced to spend over 30% of their income just to keep a roof over their heads.**
Housing is a fundamental human need. It is essential to economic opportunity, family stability, and human dignity. That is why I have spent years fighting alongside housing advocates to pass a real solution.

Late last week, we did the seemingly impossible: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law.
This landmark law cuts through partisan gridlock to:
* **Crush Wallstreet Monopolies:****** It places strict limits on large institutional investors, preventing massive corporations from outbidding everyday families on single-family homes.
* **Build More Homes:** It opens up federal funding and grants to fast-track home construction, embrace manufactured and modular housing, and slash local red tape.
* **Lower Costs:** It gives local municipalities the direct financial tools they need to make housing affordable again.

This bill passed with an overwhelming bipartisan majority. It is commonsense legislation that everyday Americans desperately need.

But Donald Trump refused to sign it.
Instead of helping families achieve the American dream, Trump called this legislation a “big yawn” and claimed it isn’t as important as his preferred bill, the SAVE Act – a dangerous piece of legislation designed to make it harder for Americans to vote.
Trump held your housing security hostage to play political games with your voting rights. He doesn’t care about you. It’s that simple.
This bill did eventually become law even without his signature. But make no mistake, Trump’s refusal to act proves exactly who he stands for – and it isn’t you.

**I will always stand on the side of everyday Americans. But to keep up this fight, protect our democratic process, and finally deliver affordable housing, I need you with me.**
[**Friend, Trump would rather constrain voting rights than give Americans adequate opportunity and accessibility to housing. Please chip in $5, $25, or whatever you can spare right now to help flip the Senate and stand against Trump’s negligence.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135462945/634305713/-1799740860?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1469-fr-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmM3NzFhYTAtZjg4MS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sBROdUNMqDQ2Dn0YHWhmn_jT-b71uYDjGqI36r02H9Q=)

subject: What do we really want for our children?
body:
It’s not what you might think...
| | **Can 't see this message? _[View in browser](https://momsforamerica.us/so/1bPzmqhqM/c?w=iiEFnpmxAsL4hZZxtsQvs9DV4FU4PGJNttAZ6vnq7HU.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9tb21zZm9yYW1lcmljYS51cy9zby8xYlB6bXFocU0_bGFuZ3VhZ2VUYWc9ZW4iLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ)_**
---
| | |
---
| | [](https://momsforamerica.us/so/1bPzmqhqM/c?w=u9lxGuaZW0GcZWMVY0V_SpYO8bBcF5LoQDtV6e1DmO0.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly8xNzc2Y2x1Yi51cy8iLCJyIjoiOWM2NDcyNmItZTNhZC00NzdiLWFmZTAtMTg2NDQ5MDg3MGViIiwibSI6Im1haWwiLCJjIjoiYjM4MzhiZjgtZmFiMC00MWI5LTk2NzMtZThjNmJlZmI2NTc3In0)
---
| | What do we want for our children? Of course, we want them to be successful and happy. We want them to have a good job and a family of their own. But what about their character? I think all of us as moms want to know our kids are good people. That’s been the case through the entire history of our nation. In 1783, while managing her family and estate alone, Abigail Adams, wife of America’s second President John Adams, wrote to her own son John Quincy Adams, “What is it that affectionate parents require of their Children for all their care, anxiety, and toil on their accounts? Only that they would be wise and virtuous, benevolent and kind.” For all we do to pour into our children’s lives, to know that they are wise, virtuous, and kind is our greatest reward.
---
| | [](https://momsforamerica.us/so/1bPzmqhqM/c?w=u1ROZh3YXffTjs7YaZRUWosm28KVNSJ8Jp6ii8D2heQ.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly8xNzc2Y2x1Yi51cyIsInIiOiI4ZjczNDgzZi1mOGVlLTQ3YjItOTdlYS03ZGQ0MzBkM2I0YTMiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ)
---
| | | [**Join the 1776 Club**](https://momsforamerica.us/so/1bPzmqhqM/c?w=8mYHJr_wAuL7tY6Hrr0YhzPG4ROEk3wLWB0GUEsSEdk.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly8xNzc2Y2x1Yi51cyIsInIiOiJkZjUxZThhZi0xMzUzLTQ4MGItOTA1YS1hZTQ4NGEzMmEwYmUiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ)
---
| | I founded Moms for America to help mothers like you raise more kind, Godly, and patriotic families. We provide resources and community to help you in that effort. But look around. This world fights us in that effort at every turn. Our children face a culture that is anything but wise, virtuous, and kind. It can be hard to compete with video games, Snapchat, and YouTube when you’re just trying to survive the stress and challenges of each day. But you’re not alone. I’m asking you to join our new 1776 Club with a donation of $17.76 a month. Your investment will help us reach out to even more moms, helping them raise the kind of kids who will make a positive difference. Help other moms know they are also not alone.
---
| |
---
| | | [**Join the 1776 Club**](https://momsforamerica.us/so/1bPzmqhqM/c?w=7m5sxOcUl0bITcezHerO9wH4alJL1c_XwH4y00qZCQI.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly8xNzc2Y2x1Yi51cyIsInIiOiJjNDk2OGRlOC03NWMzLTRiMzQtOTE2NC0zMzRjMDJlMjQ4ZjEiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ)
---
| | Abigail Adams knew it. Moms throughout our nation’s history have known it. And we know it today. Passionate and committed moms are the best hope for the future of our nation. Would you please join me today? If you do, I’ll send you a digital copy of my book “Remember the Ladies” that tells the story of the unsung women who helped found our nation. [And if you click here, you can hear me read a brand new excerpt from that book.](https://momsforamerica.us/so/1bPzmqhqM/c?w=OuI6ankVd3XdyclgB8sDs-9qJPUr7L2nw9Bh9RS4Nf4.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly8xNzc2Y2x1Yi51cy8jYm9vayIsInIiOiJiNDFlZjQwMS03MmU2LTRkMTItOGY0NC1kNTNiYzlkNjEwOTMiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ) Our country’s future is being written right now. And it’s up to us to decide what it will look like. With gratitude,Kimberly Fletcher
Founder and PresidentMoms for America®

The White House on Wednesday posted four packages of declassified and formerly internal [government records](https://substack.com/redirect/4e833b59-91bc-4dc1-9704-91ed79f455e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a document dump that runs from CIA China reporting to an FBI box of fake voter forms in western Michigan.
The documents show unequivocally that the intelligence community, during President Trump's first term but especially under President Joe Biden, actively concealed information about the extent to which China was engaged in pro-Biden clandestine activities.
Trump, in a prime time address last night, laid out what the documents reveal, stopping short of suggesting that the 2020 election was stolen or rigged. He also never alleged that actual votes were changed. But his remarks, in concert with the document release, expose the soft center of American elections, i.e. the registration database and the identity checks around it.
Here are ten items we're tracking from the Election Integrity documents...
## **1\. DHS says more than 250,000 noncitizens are illegally registered in four states -- California, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada**
The Department of Homeland Security says a review of public voter files from four states that do not use the federal SAVE citizenship-verification system turned up more than a quarter-million ineligible registrants.
"OVER 250,000 NON-CITIZENS ARE ILLEGALLY REGISTERED TO VOTE IN JUST THE FOUR STATES FOR WHICH PUBLIC DATA FILES HAVE BEEN REVIEWED," DHS states, in all capital letters, in a one-page summary titled "Preventing Alien Voting."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0d44f5a0-2074-45ce-964b-6d58c846658d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The states notified are California, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada, according to the document. DHS says it "stands ready to support their efforts to identify and remove ineligible registrants" and that the review is expanding to additional states.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..5-Xnrac6451d7oOiBUybekvxNaMIO3oc2HzE02pbizo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207438103)
Notably, Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows [has admitted](https://substack.com/redirect/58048d50-79b2-4402-a18d-a3b0d727597c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that non-citizens are registered to vote in Maine, but she has refused to turn over Maine's Central Voter Registration file to DOJ.
## **2\. In Michigan, the FBI ran 107 seized voter forms and found 91 phantoms**
In a box of voter-registration applications seized from a 2020 paid canvassing operation in Michigan, FBI database checks came back empty for the overwhelming majority.
"Database searches were conducted on the 107 voter registration applications from item 1B1 ... in an attempt to identify voter registration applications with potentially fraudulent signatures or listing non-existent individuals," the FBI electronic communication says. "Ninety-one individuals returned no results in database checks."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/132d2c80-1ad1-4980-87da-5dd63b1ce05b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Sixteen of the 107 named people existed at all. Only four had a signature on file that matched the application. The context of the intelligence document is difficult to discern, so it's not entirely clear how large the false registration scheme was.
Regardless, the document shows the FBI was aware of a large-scale effort to falsify voter registrations in a swing state but appears to have done nothing further to expose the individuals behind it.
## **3\. An unevaluated FBI report from Albany claimed China made fake U.S. driver 's licenses to cast mail-in votes for Biden**
The most explosive single page in the China package is also the one the FBI wrapped in the most warnings.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a2561643-1b6c-4672-8e43-e2e20c40691b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The FBI Intelligence Information Report, dated September 2020 and later provided to Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley, carries this banner on its face: "INFORMATION REPORT, NOT FINALLY EVALUATED INTELLIGENCE."
The subject line alleges Chinese government production and export of fraudulent U.S. driver's licenses to CCP sympathizers in the United States "in order to create tens of thousands of fraudulent mail-in votes" for Joe Biden in late August 2020. The report says China pulled real names, ID numbers and addresses from millions of TikTok accounts to make the fakes hard to detect.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c9e3a424-f7f1-43b0-94f6-5a462f01755a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |

If China is pulling address information from Tiktok accounts, that would suggest that ByteDance was turning on GPS services to track users -- which is another good reason to never download TikTok. The FBI's own comment on the same page points out the questions raised by the intel: "A persons address information was not a valid field when creating a TikTok account. It was unspecified how China would attain US address data from the application."
## **4\. A CIA note says China 's goal was to stop Trump's reelection -- and other records show analysts complaining the reporting was "massaged"**
The intelligence community lied to President Trump about China's efforts to interfere in the 2018 and 2020 elections. The memos consistently say that intelligence was "massaged," but when you review all of the memos about the handling of China-related intelligence, it's clear that the intent was to deceive Trump.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/33bc2ebe-f5a8-471d-89a9-40545a7e389e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Internal email traffic shows analysts fighting over how China-and-elections link was packaged. One message in the file complains that the National Security Agency (NSA)"deliberately massaged our one pending PDB to avoid any direct links to the election."
The National Intelligence Officer for Cyber went further, writing that the intelligence community was "deliberately avoiding mentioning a connection to elections for non-substantive reasons" and that tradecraft objections "isn't getting our work incorporated or even mentioned."
A CIA note on sensitive PRC reporting from 2018 to 2020 describes a mid-2018 Chinese Communist Party (CCP) policy to leverage domestic and foreign actors opposed to the president to reduce his votes, force his resignation or prevent his reelection. Later reporting summarized in the package describes Beijing steering resources toward swing states, pressuring Trump's financial backers and flagging journalists for negative coverage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19c76baa-06cb-4d19-a484-46f610c48e28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Ties to Maine:** China's state-run media [Xinhua reported](https://substack.com/redirect/55696b7a-576e-441a-837b-11e3f64a3b0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Jan. 2019 that then-Secretary of State Matt Dunlap was among the U.S. officials who accepted a PRC-backed trip to China. The article describes how Ping Huang, then the New Chinese Consular General in New York, visited Maine for the inauguration of Gov. Janet Mills.

Per Xinhua, Huang also [visited](https://substack.com/redirect/55696b7a-576e-441a-837b-11e3f64a3b0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Dunlap and Senate President Troy Jackson.
Jackson is now among the front-runners to receive the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination, while Dunlap is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Representative in Maine's Second Congressional District.
## **5\. Declassified tables catalog roughly 204 million U.S. voter records in datasets attributed to Chinese actors -- usable, one paper warns, to request absentee ballots for low-propensity voters**
A declassified inventory of U.S. data attributed to PRC possession leads with a single staggering line item: unspecified U.S. voter data totaling **204,822,241 records** -- 45 gigabytes, dated 2016, including names, ages, phone numbers and addresses.
The White House Government Transparency Task Force frames the wider claim this way: "The declassified intelligence reveals that voter registration rolls from at least 18 states (not all identified by name) have been compromised by the People's Republic of China," and "more than 200 million voter records were also compromised by the PRC, without state-specific affiliations."
The companion DHS threat paper spells out how those voter files could be used. The registration file often carries the exact fields needed to request a mail ballot, and that package "can support bulk absentee requests for low-propensity voters" -- the registered citizens least likely to show up and notice a ballot was pulled in their name.
Maine's Absentee Ballot request platform runs on pre-2016 antiquated software. Until recently, the site lacked even a basic "Captcha" to prevent mass, automated ballot requests.
In theory, Maine would have been ripe for the kind of mass exploitation the DHS threat paper lays out. Indeed, current large-language models would make mass requests for absentee ballots a trivial task for even a moderately skilled computer user.
## **6\. CISA testers took full control of election-office networks "within hours or days"**
The least conspiratorial document in the dump is also the hardest to wave away. From roughly 2019 to 2024, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) broke into state and local election-office networks on purpose and wrote down what it found.
"In multiple cases, CISA assessors gained full network control within hours or days," the agency's 2026 Election Report says, "demonstrating that many SLTT partners remain soft targets incapable of stopping even moderately skilled adversaries."
CISA described flat networks, shared credentials, weak multifactor authentication, **outdated operating systems** and legacy remote access left reachable from places that should have been sealed off. And it said the certification rules make it worse: "Some government election systems certification regimes require that no patches be applied for months before an election," leaving known holes open on machines about to count real votes. The result, in CISA's words: "known, documented vulnerabilities persist for months or years on production election systems."
The report doesn't say whether it was able to access Maine offices under Secretary of State Shenna Bellows.
## **7\. A Michigan witness told the FBI canvassers were paid on debit cards to register phony voters -- and thought the point was to suppress Trump's vote**
An FBI document, recorded in 2023, records how one witness in Michigan described a paid canvassing operation of more than 100 people, quotas tied to completed registrations, and pay of roughly $800 loaded onto company debit cards to compensate workers.
According to the witness, supervisors told a meeting of more than 100 workers that if they could not gather enough applications, they should "just fill them in." When someone asked what that meant, the witness said, a supervisor picked up a blank form, filled it with made-up information and said, "this is what I mean."
The instructions, subject who was interviewed, were to invent Social Security numbers, invent names, sign cursive for people who could not. The witness estimated personally submitting about 100 fake applications.
A separate July 2025 interview describes gift-card and bonus incentives, and the witness offered a personal opinion that the operation may have been trying to suppress votes for President Trump.

## **8\. The case ran about four years, stalled repeatedly at DOJ, and ended with no charges -- a slow-walk the file lays bare**
The Michigan investigation began with a city clerk's referral in October 2020 and did not close until federal prosecutors declined the case years later, after handwriting lab work stretched into 2024. Along the way, the Justice Department's Public Integrity Section used the department's election non-interference policy to control the clock.
Put together, the documents show that an investigation into well-financed large-scale voter fraud operations in a swing state was effectively killed by the Biden Administration.
"Accordingly, PIN concurs in the proposed interviews of the canvassers only after the November 7, 2023, election is concluded, certified, and uncontested," the Election Crimes Branch director wrote -- pushing roughly 100 canvasser interviews past yet another election.
It's worth pointing out that, had former Vice President Kamala Harris won the 2024 election, none of this would be public knowledge.
At least one FBI agent did not want to let go of theMichigan case.
"I'm not really comfortable closing the case at this point without raising these issues," the agent wrote, then quoted DOJ's own manual back at headquarters: even when no fraudulent votes result, "the fraudulent registrations that arise from this conduct are not victimless offenses."
## **9\. A federal threat paper says China breached state voter systems -- and warns stolen data "does not get stale"**
The second DHS document, an 11-page unclassified paper dated July 2026, highlights the threat posed by China's possession of stolen voter information.
"Recently declassified records revealed that China breached multiple state voter registration systems prior to the 2020 election," the paper says. "Unfortunately, this is not a new phenomenon."
Hackers have tried to breach registration systems in all 50 states, with confirmed successes in at least 20, according to DHS.
"Data obtained in a breach from 2021, for example, could be used to request a ballot for an election in 2028 because the data does not get stale," the paper says. An adversary can use stolen fields to request absentee ballots, or to alter and delete registrants -- change addresses, change parties, wipe records -- slowly enough to evade detection.
"The real threat is what can be done with the stolen data," the paper says.
_Paging Shenna Bellows ... Paging Shenna Bellows..._
## **10\. What the documents do not prove**
None of the four packages, on its face, establishes that certified U.S. vote tallies were altered at scale or that any presidential result was flipped. CISA's report is about fragile systems, not a stolen count. The 250,000 noncitizen figure is a headcount limited to four states. The Albany driver's-license report is stamped "not finally evaluated" and carries the FBI's own technical caveat. The Michigan file proves fake registrations and a federal non-prosecution -- not that manufactured forms became counted ballots.
However, the documents prove indisputably that actors within the federal intelligence community tried to conceal information about China's actions concerning national elections from President Donald Trump.

In a primetime address paired with a document release, President Trump made a powerful case that American elections are vulnerable to Chinese hackers -- and the CIA under Joe Biden wanted it that way. Jul 17 | | | | | | | | | | | The White House on Wednesday posted four packages of declassified and formerly internal , a document dump that runs from CIA China reporting to an FBI box of fake voter forms in western Michigan. The documents show unequivocally that the intelligence community, during President Trump's first term but especially under President Joe Biden, actively concealed information about the extent to which China was engaged in pro-Biden clandestine activities. Trump, in a prime time address last night, laid out what the documents reveal, stopping short of suggesting that the 2020 election was stolen or rigged. He also never alleged that actual votes were changed. But his remarks, in concert with the document release, expose the soft center of American elections, i.e. the registration database and the identity checks around it. Here are ten items we're tracking from the Election Integrity documents... 1\. DHS says more than 250,000 noncitizens are illegally registered in four states -- California, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada The Department of Homeland Security says a review of public voter files from four states that do not use the federal SAVE citizenship-verification system turned up more than a quarter-million ineligible registrants. "OVER 250,000 NON-CITIZENS ARE ILLEGALLY REGISTERED TO VOTE IN JUST THE FOUR STATES FOR WHICH PUBLIC DATA FILES HAVE BEEN REVIEWED," DHS states, in all capital letters, in a one-page summary titled "Preventing Alien Voting." | | ---|---|--- The states notified are California, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada, according to the document. DHS says it "stands ready to support their efforts to identify and remove ineligible registrants" and that the review is expanding to additional states. Notably, Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows that non-citizens are registered to vote in Maine, but she has refused to turn over Maine's Central Voter Registration file to DOJ. 2\. In Michigan, the FBI ran 107 seized voter forms and found 91 phantoms In a box of voter-registration applications seized from a 2020 paid canvassing operation in Michigan, FBI database checks came back empty for the overwhelming majority. "Database searches were conducted on the 107 voter registration applications from item 1B1 ... in an attempt to identify voter registration applications with potentially fraudulent signatures or listing non-existent individuals," the FBI electronic communication says. "Ninety-one individuals returned no results in database checks." | | ---|---|--- Sixteen of the 107 named people existed at all. Only four had a signature on file that matched the application. The context of the intelligence document is difficult to discern, so it's not entirely clear how large the false registration scheme was. Regardless, the document shows the FBI was aware of a large-scale effort to falsify voter registrations in a swing state but appears to have done nothing further to expose the individuals behind it. 3\. An unevaluated FBI report from Albany claimed China made fake U.S. driver 's licenses to cast mail-in votes for Biden The most explosive single page in the China package is also the one the FBI wrapped in the most warnings. | | ---|---|--- The FBI Intelligence Information Report, dated September 2020 and later provided to Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley, carries this banner on its face: "INFORMATION REPORT, NOT FINALLY EVALUATED INTELLIGENCE." The subject line alleges Chinese government production and export of fraudulent U.S. driver's licenses to CCP sympathizers in the United States "in order to create tens of thousands of fraudulent mail-in votes" for Joe Biden in late August 2020. The report says China pulled real names, ID numbers and addresses from millions of TikTok accounts to make the fakes hard to detect. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | October 1, 2025 | If China is pulling address information from Tiktok accounts, that would suggest that ByteDance was turning on GPS services to track users -- which is another good reason to never download TikTok. The FBI's own comment on the same page points out the questions raised by the intel: "A persons address information was not a valid field when creating a TikTok account. It was unspecified how China would attain US address data from the application." 4\. A CIA note says China 's goal was to stop Trump's reelection -- and other records show analysts complaining the reporting was "massaged" The intelligence community lied to President Trump about China's efforts to interfere in the 2018 and 2020 elections. The memos consistently say that intelligence was "massaged," but when you review all of the memos about the handling of China-related intelligence, it's clear that the intent was to deceive Trump. | | ---|---|--- Internal email traffic shows analysts fighting over how China-and-elections link was packaged. One message in the file complains that the National Security Agency (NSA)"deliberately massaged our one pending PDB to avoid any direct links to the election." The National Intelligence Officer for Cyber went further, writing that the intelligence community was "deliberately avoiding mentioning a connection to elections for non-substantive reasons" and that tradecraft objections "isn't getting our work incorporated or even mentioned." A CIA note on sensitive PRC reporting from 2018 to 2020 describes a mid-2018 Chinese Communist Party (CCP) policy to leverage domestic and foreign actors opposed to the president to reduce his votes, force his resignation or prevent his reelection. Later reporting summarized in the package describes Beijing steering resources toward swing states, pressuring Trump's financial backers and flagging journalists for negative coverage. | | ---|---|--- Ties to Maine: China's state-run media in Jan. 2019 that then-Secretary of State Matt Dunlap was among the U.S. officials who accepted a PRC-backed trip to China. The article describes how Ping Huang, then the New Chinese Consular General in New York, visited Maine for the inauguration of Gov. Janet Mills. Subscribe to The Robinson Report. All the cool kids do it. Per Xinhua, Huang also with Dunlap and Senate President Troy Jackson. Jackson is now among the front-runners to receive the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination, while Dunlap is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Representative in Maine's Second Congressional District. 5\. Declassified tables catalog roughly 204 million U.S. voter records in datasets attributed to Chinese actors -- usable, one paper warns, to request absentee ballots for low-propensity voters A declassified inventory of U.S. data attributed to PRC possession leads with a single staggering line item: unspecified U.S. voter data totaling 204,822,241 records -- 45 gigabytes, dated 2016, including names, ages, phone numbers and addresses. The White House Government Transparency Task Force frames the wider claim this way: "The declassified intelligence reveals that voter registration rolls from at least 18 states (not all identified by name) have been compromised by the People's Republic of China," and "more than 200 million voter records were also compromised by the PRC, without state-specific affiliations." The companion DHS threat paper spells out how those voter files could be used. The registration file often carries the exact fields needed to request a mail ballot, and that package "can support bulk absentee requests for low-propensity voters" -- the registered citizens least likely to show up and notice a ballot was pulled in their name. Maine's Absentee Ballot request platform runs on pre-2016 antiquated software. Until recently, the site lacked even a basic "Captcha" to prevent mass, automated ballot requests. In theory, Maine would have been ripe for the kind of mass exploitation the DHS threat paper lays out. Indeed, current large-language models would make mass requests for absentee ballots a trivial task for even a moderately skilled computer user. 6\. CISA testers took full control of election-office networks "within hours or days" The least conspiratorial document in the dump is also the hardest to wave away. From roughly 2019 to 2024, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) broke into state and local election-office networks on purpose and wrote down what it found. "In multiple cases, CISA assessors gained full network control within hours or days," the agency's 2026 Election Report says, "demonstrating that many SLTT partners remain soft targets incapable of stopping even moderately skilled adversaries." CISA described flat networks, shared credentials, weak multifactor authentication, outdated operating systems and legacy remote access left reachable from places that should have been sealed off. And it said the certification rules make it worse: "Some government election systems certification regimes require that no patches be applied for months before an election," leaving known holes open on machines about to count real votes. The result, in CISA's words: "known, documented vulnerabilities persist for months or years on production election systems." The report doesn't say whether it was able to access Maine offices under Secretary of State Shenna Bellows. 7\. A Michigan witness told the FBI canvassers were paid on debit cards to register phony voters -- and thought the point was to suppress Trump's vote An FBI document, recorded in 2023, records how one witness in Michigan described a paid canvassing operation of more than 100 people, quotas tied to completed registrations, and pay of roughly $800 loaded onto company debit cards to compensate workers. According to the witness, supervisors told a meeting of more than 100 workers that if they could not gather enough applications, they should "just fill them in." When someone asked what that meant, the witness said, a supervisor picked up a blank form, filled it with made-up information and said, "this is what I mean." The instructions, subject who was interviewed, were to invent Social Security numbers, invent names, sign cursive for people who could not. The witness estimated personally submitting about 100 fake applications. A separate July 2025 interview describes gift-card and bonus incentives, and the witness offered a personal opinion that the operation may have been trying to suppress votes for President Trump. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | May 21, 2025 | 8\. The case ran about four years, stalled repeatedly at DOJ, and ended with no charges -- a slow-walk the file lays bare The Michigan investigation began with a city clerk's referral in October 2020 and did not close until federal prosecutors declined the case years later, after handwriting lab work stretched into 2024. Along the way, the Justice Department's Public Integrity Section used the department's election non-interference policy to control the clock. Put together, the documents show that an investigation into well-financed large-scale voter fraud operations in a swing state was effectively killed by the Biden Administration. "Accordingly, PIN concurs in the proposed interviews of the canvassers only after the November 7, 2023, election is concluded, certified, and uncontested," the Election Crimes Branch director wrote -- pushing roughly 100 canvasser interviews past yet another election. It's worth pointing out that, had former Vice President Kamala Harris won the 2024 election, none of this would be public knowledge. At least one FBI agent did not want to let go of theMichigan case. "I'm not really comfortable closing the case at this point without raising these issues," the agent wrote, then quoted DOJ's own manual back at headquarters: even when no fraudulent votes result, "the fraudulent registrations that arise from this conduct are not victimless offenses." 9\. A federal threat paper says China breached state voter systems -- and warns stolen data "does not get stale" The second DHS document, an 11-page unclassified paper dated July 2026, highlights the threat posed by China's possession of stolen voter information. "Recently declassified records revealed that China breached multiple state voter registration systems prior to the 2020 election," the paper says. "Unfortunately, this is not a new phenomenon." Hackers have tried to breach registration systems in all 50 states, with confirmed successes in at least 20, according to DHS. "Data obtained in a breach from 2021, for example, could be used to request a ballot for an election in 2028 because the data does not get stale," the paper says. An adversary can use stolen fields to request absentee ballots, or to alter and delete registrants -- change addresses, change parties, wipe records -- slowly enough to evade detection. "The real threat is what can be done with the stolen data," the paper says. Paging Shenna Bellows ... Paging Shenna Bellows... 10\. What the documents do not prove None of the four packages, on its face, establishes that certified U.S. vote tallies were altered at scale or that any presidential result was flipped. CISA's report is about fragile systems, not a stolen count. The 250,000 noncitizen figure is a headcount limited to four states. The Albany driver's-license report is stamped "not finally evaluated" and carries the FBI's own technical caveat. The Michigan file proves fake registrations and a federal non-prosecution -- not that manufactured forms became counted ballots. However, the documents prove indisputably that actors within the federal intelligence community tried to conceal information about China's actions concerning national elections from President Donald Trump. ? * We'll have more on the Election Integrity Files on Maine Wire TV today at 4:00 pm EST, plus a review of last night Democratic Senate debates You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. Hazy skies. Smoke in the air you can taste. Extreme heat. Drought. Rising death counts.
It's not a great time for those of us--the majority of Americans, despite what the climate hushers claim--who understand that these climate disasters are a growing threat to everything we hold dear.
So it's important to take note of the victories, when they come along. That's why I wanted to share this essay I wrote for _[The New Republic](https://substack.com/redirect/ce5ebc32-adcf-45e1-ac58-3e0a3979aa14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ about a major legal victory in the fight to hold Big Oil accountable for their climate crimes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48d8d816-17e8-4792-a370-802179224b79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"The court should add this far-fetched claim to the growing list of meritless climate lawsuits the state and federal courts have already dismissed." That's how Chevron's lawyer Theodore Boutrous responded last year when Misti Leon filed a first-of-its-kind [lawsuit](https://substack.com/redirect/623305a0-cbe8-47fd-8017-41ace20bfbaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Washington State against major oil and gas companies for the wrongful death of her mother, Julie Leon, who died during the record-breaking Pacific Northwest heat dome that killed over [1,400 people](https://substack.com/redirect/e4f8bcf2-cb8f-420a-a25c-b75ac3b188a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2021.
Last week, a Washington state court published its [response](https://substack.com/redirect/6819b641-bb96-4b32-8dde-64652675f1d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Big Oil's effort to throw out Leon's "far-fetched" claim. Boutrous was no doubt disappointed, for the court rejected the defendants' motion to dismiss--meaning Misti Leon's case to hold the fossil fuel industry accountable for her mother's climate-induced death will now be proceeding toward discovery and trial.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..2SXQLMFMy0_9mTg2hKB9IrNXrZ0PiQ46K1WFfkuVRYo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207423310)
This is a big deal. First, it's striking how clearly the court ruled that Leon's pathbreaking new theory of climate accountability is "not about regulating emissions," as the defendants had argued. Leon's lawsuit alleges that Big Oil companies should be liable for her mother's death based on two state law causes of action: their failure to warn the public about the climate catastrophes they knew their fossil fuel products would cause, and their deceptive advertising--both climate denial and greenwashing--that have misled the public about these dangers for decades.
The defendants refused to accept those claims on their own terms. Big Oil's primary arguments to dismiss Leon's suit--the same arguments it is [currently pushing](https://substack.com/redirect/02b60bc5-d1a3-4456-8ce5-0f9352b90a46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the Supreme Court against a more traditional climate case--are that her case is preempted by the Clean Air Act (and also, somehow, the Constitution) and that her claims would "usurp the power of the legislative and executive branches to set climate policy."
The court's response to these claims was unequivocal: Failure to warn and deceptive advertising are state law causes of action. They are adjudicated by courts all the time. And they have nothing to do with--and are therefore not preempted by--the Clean Air Act. "This case is about a single individual and an allegation that a single weather event contributed to her untimely passing," the court wrote. "It is seeking damages for her death and nothing else"--pointedly, damages that are "not an attempt to regulate future emissions." Such claims are not preempted because the Clean Air Act "does not address product liability or deceptive marketing." And they are not non-justiciable political questions because they are "simple torts" that do not "implicate separation-of-powers concerns." This ruling is a major boon to Leon's new legal theory.
Naturally, surviving a motion to dismiss doesn't mean a case will succeed--not by a long shot. But this ruling confirms that such a lawsuit is legally plausible. The court essentially asks if there would be a cognizable claim if it accepted the plaintiff's factual allegations as true. If one has confidence in Leon's allegations--regarding Big Oil's climate deception, the role of this deception in furthering climate change, and the impact of climate change on heat waves like the Pacific Northwest heat dome--then there is every reason to believe that a judge's gatekeeping regarding these legal questions is as big an obstacle to a suit like Leon's as the willingness of a jury of regular people to respond to evidence of Big Oil's deception by ruling in favor of a bereaved daughter like Misti Leon.
As such, this ruling could encourage other victims of climate disasters to file their own wrongful death suits against Big Oil--and it could give other plaintiffs' attorneys confidence to take on these cases. That should make the fossil fuel industry very nervous. Julie Leon is far from the only victim of Big Oil's climate misconduct. Dozens of people in New Jersey and Philadelphia were just [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/e14612bc-326d-4bf9-9463-eb1652b315be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Fourth of July heat wave, which climate scientists have already [determined](https://substack.com/redirect/e043bb36-4217-4d89-9215-aa9682aa3d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would have been "virtually impossible" but for climate change. Maricopa County, Arizona, experienced [430 heat-related deaths](https://substack.com/redirect/e4b7a618-ec67-4e0e-9961-e99d7cb16b9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2025, and its death count this year is [outpacing](https://substack.com/redirect/1f4b3edd-d889-4b46-a70d-0d9df8475898?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that figure "at a troubling rate." Figures like these could be on track to explode in the near future. Already, some regions are experiencing orders of magnitude more carnage--a recent [analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/fe3b81ef-7dd6-4e30-9ed8-5c4af3112f46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that extreme heat from climate change may have caused over 20,000 deaths in Europe last month alone.
The progression of Leon's case could also help inspire a powerful and previously untapped category of legal actors to join the fight for climate accountability: prosecutors. Though criminal prosecution requires a higher burden of proof than civil litigation, the core legal argument being made by Misti Leon is similar to the one prosecutors would rely on to charge Big Oil companies with criminal offenses--like [homicide](https://substack.com/redirect/bb3e7d16-c2a2-48bc-ac15-80624a111dbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [reckless endangerment](https://substack.com/redirect/8b631728-be37-4d2d-97fe-801c18092e3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or [risking catastrophe](https://substack.com/redirect/acedc54f-8ba9-4615-ab8f-eac35a121c48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--in relation to the climate disasters that are, in some instances, killing [more](https://substack.com/redirect/caf9dd83-d8b5-4c12-a597-2b08971264ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of their constituents than are being lost to traditional homicides.
It seems the fossil fuel industry is becoming concerned about this possibility. The latest draft [legislation](https://substack.com/redirect/083f7901-4b1c-4c21-a1b9-72f298413854?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) being put forward by the American Legislative Exchange Council to immunize oil and gas companies from liability for climate harms includes language creating a shield for all "criminal charges, indictments, or prosecutions based on or arising from" Big Oil's climate-related misconduct.
Corporations like ExxonMobil, Chevron, Shell, and BP are desperately looking for get-out-of-jail-free cards like these because they know that claims like those of Misti Leon are not, in fact, "far-fetched" or "meritless," as Boutrous bluffed. They know that people like Julie Leon should not be losing their lives. People like Misti should not be losing their mothers. These are not natural tragedies. They're the result of the conduct of a small number of companies that knew their fossil fuels would cause, in their own words, "[globally catastrophic](https://substack.com/redirect/3f6d10df-12f7-49dd-bb9b-4af84354174f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" climate harms that would create "more violent weather" and cause "suffering and death due to thermal extremes." Despite this knowledge, they spent years preventing the public from understanding the risks their products were creating, in order to protect their obscene profits.
These companies have blood on their hands. The volume of that blood is growing every year. Following this latest court decision, they are one step closer to being held accountable for their lethal conduct. And it's all thanks to the courage of Misti Leon, a regular person going up against some of the most powerful corporations on the planet to win justice for her mother. For now, at least, she's winning.

It's not a great time for those of us--the majority of Americans, despite what the climate hushers claim--who understand that these climate disasters are a growing threat to everything we hold dear. That's how Chevron's lawyer Theodore Boutrous responded last year when Misti Leon filed a first-of-its-kind in Washington State against major oil and gas companies for the wrongful death of her mother, Julie Leon, who died during the record-breaking Pacific Northwest heat dome that killed over in 2021. Last week, a Washington state court published its to Big Oil's effort to throw out Leon's "far-fetched" claim. Boutrous was no doubt disappointed, for the court rejected the defendants' motion to dismiss--meaning Misti Leon's case to hold the fossil fuel industry accountable for her mother's climate-induced death will now be proceeding toward discovery and trial. This is a big deal. First, it's striking how clearly the court ruled that Leon's pathbreaking new theory of climate accountability is "not about regulating emissions," as the defendants had argued. Leon's lawsuit alleges that Big Oil companies should be liable for her mother's death based on two state law causes of action: their failure to warn the public about the climate catastrophes they knew their fossil fuel products would cause, and their deceptive advertising--both climate denial and greenwashing--that have misled the public about these dangers for decades.
