body:
Minnesotans deserve real leaders in Congress who are unafraid to make tough calls with moral clarity.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2370%2E791427%2E7Jqx6E)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jul26.gZgURP&refcode=em260717-1-180&t=2&akid=2370%2E791427%2E7Jqx6E)
Friend, Ilhan Omar has called to abolish ICE for years now.
One of her opponents in this race, however, has not joined that call. In fact, she was a prosecutor for ICE during Trump’s current term in the White House, while ICE agents were terrorizing our communities and rounding up our neighbors.
**Minnesotans deserve progressive leaders in Congress who are unafraid to make tough calls with moral clarity.** That’s Ilhan.
We all watched with horror as ICE descended upon Minnesota with the express goal of causing chaos, wreacking havoc, and getting revenge against communities that don’t support Donald Trump.
We all saw the videos of protesters being violently abused. Of people of color getting racially profiled. Of innocent people being dragged out of their cars and beaten. Of legal immigrants and citizens alike getting whisked away to inhumane detention centers. Of Renee Good and Alex Pretti being shot dead in the streets. Of Trump and JD Vance defending these killings and refusing to even investigate.
After all of that, after everything our communities have been through, if you can’t bring yourself to say that ICE must be abolished, **then we should have no confidence in your ability to do the right thing, even when it’s hard.**
Ilhan has earned the trust of this community because she doesn’t back down from the hard fights. She dives in head first and fights the MAGA far-right with everything she’s got.
So, with Election Day in Minnesota just weeks away:

Peter,
Six years ago today, Rep. John Lewis succumbed to cancer after a long life of “good trouble.” Rep. Lewis put his voice and his body on the line to secure voting rights. Last night, Donald Trump went on the airwaves in his latest campaign _against_ voting rights. The architect of the January 6th attack wants to rewrite voting laws just months away from an election he thinks his party will lose―and that could finally result in accountability for his corruption. And then today, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin threatened to withhold federal funding from states who don’t submit to voter purges and other forms of suppression. **[This isn’t what John Lewis spent his life fighting for. This weekend, we’re showing that Good Trouble Lives On! “ This is not about how fast California counts ballots ,” Becker said. “ All that [Trump] cares about is whether he wins or loses. And if he loses, he’ll create a fiction in his head to tell him otherwise .”
This is all a preview of what's to come in November, and it shows us how critical our work to protect mail-in ballots and inform voters is.

“ The Dumocrats, right before our very eyes, are stealing the Vote ,” Trump posted in response on social media. Vice President JD Vance, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.), and numerous other GOP leaders have likewise raised suspicion about the count without any proof of wrongdoing or concrete examples of problems.
This won't just bring up problems with the mail-in ballots themselves, but could also lead to a flood of post-election litigation, as opponents of voting rights, alleging fraud or the potential for it, pull out the stops to get votes thrown out and to contest results.
We have to step up and stop this election denialism and subversion before it gains a foothold. Our fundamental right to vote depends on it.

body:
I ran for Congress to fight for all of our neighbors, in every corner of Delaware.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3564%2E21716%2EcFW9Ox)
**The filing deadline has passed, and it’s official: I am your Democratic nominee to represent Delaware in the House of Representatives.**
I ran for Congress to fight for all of our neighbors, in every corner of Delaware. That’s why I recently launched my re-election campaign by visiting all 57 towns and cities in just 57 hours.
From Ardentown to Rehoboth Beach, I got to visit everywhere, talk to Delawareans about what they need from Congress, and learn more about what I can do to fight for working families across our state.
It’s been an honor to fight for you in the House throughout my first term. **And I’m going to keep fighting every single day, but I’m going to need your help to do it.**
If we’re going to flip the House in this year’s midterms so that we can hold this administration accountable and pass a budget that centers the needs of regular Delawareans over Trump and his billionaire allies, it has to start by keeping this seat blue.
**Our campaign is powered by everyday people, which is why today,[I’m asking you to pitch in $20.26, or whatever amount you can, to help me win re-election, flip the House, and keep up the fight for working families up and down our state.](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1469?c0=mcb-em-20260717-1.6rdoOs&refcode=em20260717-3564&t=2&akid=3564%2E21716%2EcFW9Ox)**

But we can’t do it without your support. Republicans are spending tens of millions of dollars to hold their majority, and your grassroots support is going to be the thing that helps us fight back. **[Trump wants to silence us by taking away our right to vote. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. ## Hey, Angry Patriots.
We're trying a new article format inspired by a few Substacks we follow, including The Rooster and its Mailbag series. We're calling ours **The Angry Files**.

## Election Fraud?
Donald Trump said there was election fraud and outside interference in the 2020 election. He recently released declassified intelligence documents from agencies including the CIA, NSA, and ODNI that he says support those claims. I uploaded the documents from the White House so anyone can read them and come to their own conclusions.
Some of the broad themes that appear throughout the documents include:
* Intelligence reporting discusses foreign influence efforts by countries including China, Russia, and Iran aimed at shaping U.S. politics and public opinion.
* Several documents reference concerns over foreign access to voter registration data and other sensitive election-related information.
* Internal emails show disagreements among intelligence officials over how foreign election-related activity should be analyzed and described in official assessments.
* The released material includes intelligence assessments, internal emails, and heavily redacted reports, but much of the underlying evidence remains redacted or unavailable for independent verification.

With extraordinary claims comes extraordinary evidence.
[Download White House Files](https://substack.com/redirect/88bbaaaa-5c8b-45a2-a7e4-7c41e69ab86a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm not going to dismiss this because it's Donald Trump. I'm also not going to embrace it because **it is** Donald Trump.
Words on a page are not enough. Redacted intelligence reports are not enough.
I want digital fingerprints. Digital evidence. I want independent cybersecurity experts and third-party investigators, working separately, arriving at the same conclusions.
Until then, I'm staying agnostic. Open-minded. Cautious. Paying attention. Head on a swivel. But I'm not jumping to either side without evidence.
What are your thoughts?

One thing Dani and I have talked about at length is the nonstop whataboutism coming from every side of every political argument. Instead of substance, constructive thought, or even a real understanding of the issue, we get people screaming about what the other side did first or did worse.
That does not move anything forward. It just keeps us stuck blaming the other team while lowering our own ethical, moral, and behavioral standards because they stooped to a new low.
At some point, we have to ask: What do we actually believe? What are we willing to defend? And what would incremental improvement even look like?

## Flock No?
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/001b0475-70cd-4a1c-a5a5-1db5f79e57b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This week, Cleveland City Council voted **9-6** to keep the city's Flock license-plate reader cameras for another six months.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ccd091a0-5ec4-4e51-9f21-f914c049a893?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The problem is not that Cleveland wants to reduce crime. Cleveland has real crime problems, and residents deserve safety. The problem is handing over more of our privacy to a private surveillance company that collects and stores data about where people drive and when.
Council did add restrictions, including cutting off the Northeast Ohio Regional Fusion Center's access to Cleveland's Flock data. But this still deserves serious scrutiny. We should not casually accept a future where private companies build searchable databases of our movements and call it public safety.

### What I'm Watching
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/001b0475-70cd-4a1c-a5a5-1db5f79e57b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I used to write a lot more about movies, television, and media. I may start doing that again, especially because so much of it eventually connects back to politics, culture, and how we think through the world.
There are two shows and one movie on my mind right now.
**First, watch** _**The Orville**_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aca57ade-f75d-460e-8927-ace09ae2d4e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The Orville_
It is not officially a _Star Trek_ spinoff, but let's be honest, it is a full-on love letter to what made _Star Trek_ great. Episodic stories. Characters you get to know. Ethical dilemmas where there is no clean answer and both choices can be awful in their own way. The trolly problem!
That was the brilliance of the original series, _The Next Generation_ , _Deep Space Nine_ , and _Voyager_. The best episodes did not lecture you. They gave you a problem, showed you multiple perspectives, and let you walk away thinking about it. Ten people could watch the same episode and have ten different opinions afterward.
That is what _The Orville_ does well. Season one starts out more comedic, but by season three it becomes a serious, thoughtful science-fiction show. If you love old-school _Star Trek_ , you should watch it. In my opinion, it is modern _Star Trek_ , more than modern _Star Trek_.
**The second** is _For All Mankind_. It asks a simple question: What if the space race never really ended? What if we kept pushing human exploration, science, and technological advancement through all the political conflict, mistakes, costs, and human drama?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ab3dc181-e411-47e6-8a6f-2a5481c48318?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_For All Mankind_
The show can drift into more drama than I personally want at times, but the bigger idea is worth it. It gives you hope and wonder about what humanity might be capable of if we actually decided to put our minds and resources toward exploration. It does not feel like some impossible warp-speed fantasy. Much of it feels close enough to reality that it makes you ask why we stopped dreaming that big.
**And finally** , Christopher Nolan's _The Odyssey_ comes out this week.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/10772a14-a2ec-4baf-97bc-aaf0d4289d2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The Odyssey_
There has already been plenty of online chatter trying to tear it down over casting and everything else people can find to fight about. But Christopher Nolan is one of the best directors of our generation, and, in my opinion, one of the best ever. His movies are not perfect. No movie is if you look hard enough. But the early reactions have me hopeful that this is going to be the epic people have been waiting for.
We (Laura and I) are seeing it this weekend. We will report back.

A young Manchester five-piece who came up through TikTok and turned out to be the real thing. Their EP _When The Lights Are Out_ is out now, with a debut album, _Something Real_ , due this year. Frontman Cai Alty writes straight at the modern world -- climate dread, mental health, male suicide, the low hum of everyone's rage -- over guitars that earn the Arctic Monkeys and Sam Fender comparisons without hiding behind them. Rolling Stone UK called the title track "reminiscent of Humbug-era Arctic Monkeys." If you like a band that still believes a song can mean something, start here. Stay Angry. wrote an article arguing that the Democratic Party & new effort to win back men is mostly vibes. Even the candidate said so. There has been plenty of pushback online. People called her bitter and tried to turn the whole thing into a personal grievance. But what Laura wrote was also something we saw firsthand during the primary. Laura was 100% right to write that article. We are not going to keep rehashing the same arguments or replying to every person online, so you will not get every back-and-forth in your inbox. But if you want to know what I think about the Democratic Party's inauthentic push to win back white men, or men generally, read this. The Whisper Campaign The other day, The Atlantic published an article about Brian Poindexter, the Democratic candidate for Congress in Ohio's 7th District. The title was "The Return of the Democratic Manly Man," and the subtitle announced that the party has a new campaign strategy: masculinity... 5 hours ago The Angry Democrat and Matt Diemer Election Fraud? Donald Trump said there was election fraud and outside interference in the 2020 election. He recently released declassified intelligence documents from agencies including the CIA, NSA, and ODNI that he says support those claims. I uploaded the documents from the White House so anyone can read them and come to their own conclusions. Some of the broad themes that appear throughout the documents include: Intelligence reporting discusses foreign influence efforts by countries including China, Russia, and Iran aimed at shaping U.S. politics and public opinion. Several documents reference concerns over foreign access to voter registration data and other sensitive election-related information. Internal emails show disagreements among intelligence officials over how foreign election-related activity should be analyzed and described in official assessments. The released material includes intelligence assessments, internal emails, and heavily redacted reports, but much of the underlying evidence remains redacted or unavailable for independent verification. With extraordinary claims comes extraordinary evidence. I'm not going to dismiss this because it's Donald Trump. I'm also not going to embrace it because it is Donald Trump. Words on a page are not enough. Redacted intelligence reports are not enough. I want digital fingerprints. Digital evidence. I want independent cybersecurity experts and third-party investigators, working separately, arriving at the same conclusions. Until then, I'm staying agnostic. Open-minded. Cautious. Paying attention. Head on a swivel. But I'm not jumping to either side without evidence. What are your thoughts? When Debate Dies This next piece comes from One thing Dani and I have talked about at length is the nonstop whataboutism coming from every side of every political argument. Instead of substance, constructive thought, or even a real understanding of the issue, we get people screaming about what the other side did first or did worse. That does not move anything forward. It just keeps us stuck blaming the other team while lowering our own ethical, moral, and behavioral standards because they stooped to a new low. At some point, we have to ask: What do we actually believe? What are we willing to defend? And what would incremental improvement even look like? What are your thoughts on Dani's article? | | and | | ---|---|--- | 4:07 PM | The Rooster is one of my daily go-tos when I want to see what is happening in other parts of Ohio. He occasionally covers Northeast Ohio too, which I always appreciate. Check out his Mailbag, where he puts several different thoughts and updates into one post. I especially wanted to point out his coverage of races around the state, where he highlights the candidates, the race, and the Democrat on the ticket. Always worth a read. The Rooster WARREN COUNTY -- I saw The Odyssey last night. I had never considered that Odysseus might have felt bad for tricking the Trojans like that... 13 hours ago 14 likes 5 comments D.J. Byrnes This next piece comes from Andrey J. Martinichin , a write-in congressional candidate in Ohio's 7th District. Andrey takes a hard look at private equity's growing role in nursing education, including how for-profit schools can load aspiring nurses with massive debt while offering programs that may leave them with limited options afterward. It is a sharp piece on what happens when Wall Street sees people trying to better their lives as a business opportunity. The Angry Ohioans U.S. healthcare is a sprawling mess, and there's no clean place to point and say "this is where it broke." So I picked a starting point that made sense to me: the classroom, where most healthcare careers begin. My background is in nursing, so that's the lens I'll use -- and what I found is a system where private equity is quietly reshaping, and warping, ... 5 hours ago The Angry Democrat and Andrey J. Martinichin Flock No? This week, Cleveland City Council voted 9-6 to keep the city's Flock license-plate reader cameras for another six months. | | ---|---|--- The problem is not that Cleveland wants to reduce crime. Cleveland has real crime problems, and residents deserve safety. The problem is handing over more of our privacy to a private surveillance company that collects and stores data about where people drive and when. Council did add restrictions, including cutting off the Northeast Ohio Regional Fusion Center's access to Cleveland's Flock data. But this still deserves serious scrutiny. We should not casually accept a future where private companies build searchable databases of our movements and call it public safety. Voted yes to extend Flock Joseph T. Tell them what you think about how they voted. Holding them accountable matters. What I'm Watching I used to write a lot more about movies, television, and media. I may start doing that again, especially because so much of it eventually connects back to politics, culture, and how we think through the world. There are two shows and one movie on my mind right now. First, watch The Orville. | | ---|---|--- The Orville It is not officially a Star Trek spinoff, but let's be honest, it is a full-on love letter to what made Star Trek great. Episodic stories. Characters you get to know. Ethical dilemmas where there is no clean answer and both choices can be awful in their own way. The trolly problem! That was the brilliance of the original series, The Next Generation , Deep Space Nine , and Voyager. The best episodes did not lecture you. They gave you a problem, showed you multiple perspectives, and let you walk away thinking about it. Ten people could watch the same episode and have ten different opinions afterward. That is what The Orville does well. Season one starts out more comedic, but by season three it becomes a serious, thoughtful science-fiction show. If you love old-school Star Trek , you should watch it. In my opinion, it is modern Star Trek , more than modern Star Trek. The second is For All Mankind. It asks a simple question: What if the space race never really ended? What if we kept pushing human exploration, science, and technological advancement through all the political conflict, mistakes, costs, and human drama? | | ---|---|--- For All Mankind The show can drift into more drama than I personally want at times, but the bigger idea is worth it. It gives you hope and wonder about what humanity might be capable of if we actually decided to put our minds and resources toward exploration. It does not feel like some impossible warp-speed fantasy. Much of it feels close enough to reality that it makes you ask why we stopped dreaming that big. And finally , Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey comes out this week. | | ---|---|--- The Odyssey There has already been plenty of online chatter trying to tear it down over casting and everything else people can find to fight about. But Christopher Nolan is one of the best directors of our generation, and, in my opinion, one of the best ever. His movies are not perfect. No movie is if you look hard enough. But the early reactions have me hopeful that this is going to be the epic people have been waiting for. We (Laura and I) are seeing it this weekend. We will report back. What Laura's Listening To I'm an audiophile, play multiple instruments (guitar, piano, drums), and am surprised I am not in a band at this point. But here's what's spinning on my record player: | | ---|---|--- A band from Manchester (a.k.a. the home of Morrissey and the Smiths). I hear a little bit of them mixed in with some mid-90s Oasis. -- on heavy rotation A young Manchester five-piece who came up through TikTok and turned out to be the real thing. Their EP When The Lights Are Out is out now, with a debut album, Something Real , due this year. Frontman Cai Alty writes straight at the modern world -- climate dread, mental health, male suicide, the low hum of everyone's rage -- over guitars that earn the Arctic Monkeys and Sam Fender comparisons without hiding behind them. Rolling Stone UK called the title track "reminiscent of Humbug-era Arctic Monkeys." If you like a band that still believes a song can mean something, start here. If you were an Oasis fan or like the Smiths or Morrissey, this music is melodic and relatable. Start with: "Something Real," "Weatherman," "Ruine" Listen: | | ---|---|--- Holy shit, they're good!! -- my new-old discovery How I slept on this LA band for this long, I can't tell you. "Sometime Around Midnight" is the gateway -- a slow-building, string-laced crescendo gut-punch about seeing an ex across a bar that goes exactly where you're afraid it will. Behind it is a whole catalog, from 2008's self-titled debut through 2024's Glory , with literate, big-hearted rock led by Mikel Jollett (also worth knowing as the author of the memoir Hollywood Park). Come for the one song everyone knows; stay for the four you'll wish you'd found sooner. Start with: "Sometime Around Midnight," "All I Ever Wanted," "Faithless," "Wishing Well" Listen: | | ---|---|--- Somebody told me....this album has a steel guitar :( -- listening with one eyebrow raised Full disclosure: I'm not a country fan. I am a Killers diehard who'll argue they're the best rock band of the last twenty-five years. So this one's a test of faith. Flowers' first solo record in eleven years (out August 21) is a full country-western turn -- cut at Nashville's historic RCA Studio A with pedal steel, harmonica, and the ghosts of Johnny Cash and Waylon Jennings, songs about family, loss, and small-town Utah. The lead single "Plans" is out now. I'm going in skeptical and hopeful in equal measure. Report to follow. Start with: "Plans" (before you judge) Listen: I hope you enjoyed this format instead of getting blasted with a separate email for every story. Take your time, bookmark the pieces that interest you, and read through them when you can. We would love your feedback. Email us at , or email me directly at . And, of course, please support our work. We spend hours every week, and honestly most of my day, looking into stories, talking to people, and figuring out how to cover more Northeast Ohio politics. Thank you for supporting us and for being an Angry Democrat. Stay Angry. Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS by supporting Matt's and Laura's work. We covered a lot of ground, from the cost of living, to housing, health care, education, and what it will take to make Vermont work better for families and communities across our state.
**I also got to talk about the kind of leadership I would bring to the governor’s office.**
I’ve spent my career taking on systems that were not working, bringing people together around big goals, and pushing until we delivered the change that Vermonters deserve. That experience has taught me that Vermont does not have to settle for small fixes or accept that our biggest challenges are simply too hard to solve.
We can make this state more affordable. We can build more housing. We can lower health care costs. We can strengthen our schools and invest in the transformational power of education.
That is what this campaign is about, and I’d love for you to hear more.

I also got to talk about the kind of leadership I would bring to the governor’s office. I’ve spent my career taking on systems that were not working, bringing people together around big goals, and pushing until we delivered the change that Vermonters deserve. That experience has taught me that Vermont does not have to settle for small fixes or accept that our biggest challenges are simply too hard to solve. We can make this state more affordable. We can build more housing. We can lower health care costs. We can strengthen our schools and invest in the transformational power of education. That is what this campaign is about, and I’d love for you to hear more. body:
I have something to say.

| Hi there, it's Jane. There’s an old saying I think about often: **_If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together._** _This movement is proof it’s true._ This primary season, our climate champions went up against big corporate money and the fossil fuel lobby in states like Pennsylvania, New Mexico, Arizona, California, and Colorado, and they won. That doesn't happen without people like you. It just doesn't. Every one of those wins started the same way: with regular people deciding they'd had enough of letting polluters and Big Money buy our elections. But this fight is just getting started. Everything we care about, from a livable planet to a democracy worth passing on, runs straight through November. Flipping the House is our shot to put a real check on Trump and the fossil fuel billionaires writing his agenda. **By Wendy M. Yurgo**
When I wrote **[The Summer of Love](https://substack.com/redirect/b7f12317-824c-4abe-8e28-d73341d7804b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a couple of weeks ago, I believed I understood what I had witnessed. Looking back, I realize I had only captured what was happening on the surface.
The story I told was about the extraordinary convergence of America's 250th birthday and the FIFA World Cup. History had created a moment no one could have planned. As our nation celebrated two and a half centuries of freedom, millions arrived from every corner of the world expecting to watch football. Instead, they became part of America's birthday celebration. They celebrated with us, laughed with us and, whether they realized it or not, became part of one of the most remarkable summers in our nation's history.
That was the Summer of Love.
Yet after the article was published, one observation kept following me.
"This isn't what I expected."
At first, I took it as a compliment to American hospitality. Then I began asking a much deeper question. Expected based on what?
The more I thought about it, the more another question emerged. How could millions of people from different countries, speaking different languages and representing vastly different cultures, all arrive with remarkably similar expectations about America?
That isn't a coincidence. It is the power of narrative.
The answer, I believe, reveals the real story of this extraordinary summer.
They came expecting one America. They found another.

_**(Piece continues)**_
For years, international audiences have been presented with an increasingly dark portrait of the United States under President Donald Trump. In my view, America was portrayed as angry, dangerous, intolerant, culturally barren and hopelessly divided. It was presented not as an imperfect but extraordinary republic, but as a warning to the world. President Trump was cast not merely as a controversial leader, but as the personification of a cruel and unwelcoming nation.
In the months leading up to the World Cup, those themes intensified. Reports focused heavily on immigration enforcement, visa restrictions, gun violence and political unrest. Some supporters chose not to travel because they feared what they believed they would encounter. Even before the opening match, much of the conversation surrounding the tournament centered not on football, but on whether visitors would feel welcome in America.
Some of those concerns reflected real issues. Visa hurdles, rising travel costs and heightened security were legitimate challenges. But they were never the whole story.
The fans came anyway.
They stepped off airplanes carrying flags, scarves and expectations shaped by years of headlines. They entered airports they had been led to believe might feel hostile. They walked streets they had been told were unsafe. They met Americans many had already been conditioned to view with suspicion.
Then something happened.
Not because of a government campaign. Not because of a White House speech. Not because of a carefully crafted public relations effort.
It happened because reality has a way of speaking for itself.
The stories began pouring in. Reuters documented the shift as supporters described experiences that differed dramatically from what they expected. A Scottish supporter in Boston recalled local women repeatedly welcoming her, saying, "They loved us, we loved them." A British fan in Miami said the America he encountered bore no resemblance to the country he had imagined from years of media coverage. A German supporter was moved to tears by the kindness shown to him. Across social media, visitors shared stories about American hospitality, customer service, neighborhood restaurants, roadside attractions and complete strangers who simply wanted to know where they were from.
These people saw America without an editor standing between them and reality.
That is why this experience matters. Media narratives hold tremendous influence, particularly over people who have never had the opportunity to experience a country for themselves. When the loudest stories consistently focus on a nation's worst moments, it becomes easy to mistake the exception for the rule and the fragment for the whole.

_**(Piece continues)**_
America is not a cable news segment. It is more than 340 million people spread across a vast and varied nation. It is cities and farms. Immigrants and families whose roots stretch back generations. It is disagreement and unity, success and failure, struggle and hope. It has real problems, as every nation does. It also possesses generosity, resilience, patriotism, humor and an instinctive willingness to welcome people from around the world.
This summer, millions encountered the America that rarely makes international headlines. The America that helps a stranger lift a suitcase. The America that buys a visitor lunch. The America that patiently explains a menu, offers directions, recommends a neighborhood restaurant and welcomes someone wearing another nation's colors.
None of this erases legitimate criticisms of the United States or suggests every visitor had a perfect experience. Nor does it mean anyone returned home sharing the same political views. That isn't the point.
The point is that millions arrived expecting one country and experienced another. The caricature collided with reality. Reality is winning.
There is an irony that should not be lost on any of us. Some of the same outlets that spent months questioning whether America could successfully welcome the world are now reporting on the warmth and hospitality visitors experienced after they arrived.
When these visitors return home, they will once again encounter familiar headlines and familiar narratives about the United States. The difference is that they now possess something they didn't have before. Their own experience.
No headline can take that away. No commentary can erase it. No one can convince someone they imagined what they personally lived.
Last week I wrote about America's birthday party. This week I'm writing about what happened after the guests arrived. They came believing what they had been told. They left believing what they had seen.
There is a profound difference between the two.
And perhaps that will become the most enduring legacy of the Summer of Love.

(Piece continues) For years, international audiences have been presented with an increasingly dark portrait of the United States under President Donald Trump. In my view, America was portrayed as angry, dangerous, intolerant, culturally barren and hopelessly divided. It was presented not as an imperfect but extraordinary republic, but as a warning to the world. President Trump was cast not merely as a controversial leader, but as the personification of a cruel and unwelcoming nation. In the months leading up to the World Cup, those themes intensified. Reports focused heavily on immigration enforcement, visa restrictions, gun violence and political unrest. Some supporters chose not to travel because they feared what they believed they would encounter. Even before the opening match, much of the conversation surrounding the tournament centered not on football, but on whether visitors would feel welcome in America. Some of those concerns reflected real issues. Visa hurdles, rising travel costs and heightened security were legitimate challenges. But they were never the whole story. The fans came anyway. They stepped off airplanes carrying flags, scarves and expectations shaped by years of headlines. They entered airports they had been led to believe might feel hostile. They walked streets they had been told were unsafe. They met Americans many had already been conditioned to view with suspicion. Then something happened. Not because of a government campaign. Not because of a White House speech. Not because of a carefully crafted public relations effort. It happened because reality has a way of speaking for itself. The stories began pouring in. Reuters documented the shift as supporters described experiences that differed dramatically from what they expected. A Scottish supporter in Boston recalled local women repeatedly welcoming her, saying, "They loved us, we loved them." A British fan in Miami said the America he encountered bore no resemblance to the country he had imagined from years of media coverage. A German supporter was moved to tears by the kindness shown to him. Across social media, visitors shared stories about American hospitality, customer service, neighborhood restaurants, roadside attractions and complete strangers who simply wanted to know where they were from. These people saw America without an editor standing between them and reality. That is why this experience matters. Media narratives hold tremendous influence, particularly over people who have never had the opportunity to experience a country for themselves. When the loudest stories consistently focus on a nation's worst moments, it becomes easy to mistake the exception for the rule and the fragment for the whole. (Piece continues below) Are you enjoying PolitiBrawl 's bold and ruthless coverage? With 1.5 million daily readers, PolitiBrawl is now the largest conservative publication on Substack! We didn't get that way by pulling our punches! on information. If we are going to take back our country, we must win the media wars. It is not an option. President Trump agrees. | | ---|---|--- will be used to FAIRLY cover President Trump's administration and aggressively hold the Democrats accountable because God knows CNN and the New York Times won't do it! This is why CNN hates us, because we are waking up more American's every day to their lies. Thank you for your support and for joining the fight alongside us. \- The PolitiBrawl Editors (Piece continues) America is not a cable news segment. It is more than 340 million people spread across a vast and varied nation. It is cities and farms. Immigrants and families whose roots stretch back generations. It is disagreement and unity, success and failure, struggle and hope. It has real problems, as every nation does. It also possesses generosity, resilience, patriotism, humor and an instinctive willingness to welcome people from around the world. This summer, millions encountered the America that rarely makes international headlines. The America that helps a stranger lift a suitcase. The America that buys a visitor lunch. The America that patiently explains a menu, offers directions, recommends a neighborhood restaurant and welcomes someone wearing another nation's colors. None of this erases legitimate criticisms of the United States or suggests every visitor had a perfect experience. Nor does it mean anyone returned home sharing the same political views. That isn't the point. The point is that millions arrived expecting one country and experienced another. The caricature collided with reality. Reality is winning. There is an irony that should not be lost on any of us. Some of the same outlets that spent months questioning whether America could successfully welcome the world are now reporting on the warmth and hospitality visitors experienced after they arrived. When these visitors return home, they will once again encounter familiar headlines and familiar narratives about the United States. The difference is that they now possess something they didn't have before. Their own experience. No headline can take that away. No commentary can erase it. No one can convince someone they imagined what they personally lived. Last week I wrote about America's birthday party. This week I'm writing about what happened after the guests arrived. They came believing what they had been told. They left believing what they had seen. There is a profound difference between the two. And perhaps that will become the most enduring legacy of the Summer of Love. About the Author Wendy M. Digging into campaign finance
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260717-3044)
Peter,
This week, I got to share that our campaign**raised over $1.1 million dollars.** Tonight, I wanted to take a step back and go through what this means for us, and where we go from here.
There’s a lot I could highlight, but I want to first thank you all for showing up for me. You make our movement possible, and [I hope you’ll keep supporting us through the final month.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260716.rnaUk1&refcode=em20260717-3044&t=1&akid=3044%2E105371%2Exs7kkB)
I’ve promised that I won’t take corporate PAC money. I won’t cater to the millionaire and billionaire class. And I’ve always believed that this campaign won’t need any of that to succeed.
Or numbers proved that. Here’s what they say:
**We’re people powered.**
* **22,792** donations—the most of any candidate in the race, _including Tom Tiffany_
* **13,323 unique donors —the most of any candidate in the race, _including Tom Tiffany_**
* **41%** of everyone who has given to a Democrat in this primary has given to Hong
* **9,455** Wisconsin donors—the most of any candidate in the race, _including Tom Tiffany_

[__](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260716.rnaUk1&refcode=em20260717-3044&t=2&akid=3044%2E105371%2Exs7kkB)
**We refused to compromise our values.**
* **0.5%** of our money comes from PACs (advocacy groups) and other organizations
* **$47** average donation—the lowest average contribution rate of any candidate in this race, _including Tom Tiffany_
* _**76%** of our money comes from inside Wisconsin_

**We have the momentum.**
* **$1,075,774 was our total raised by the end of June**
* **45%****of everything we’ve raised** came in May and June alone

There was a lot of chatter about my potential fundraising numbers and lack of allegiance to the donor class. Pundits and the media debated which of my opponents had the money and momentum to overtake my lead.
I can now offer them an answer, one they probably didn’t consider: _I_ have the money, and _I_ have the momentum. And I got here without compromising the values of this campaign.
I’ve been emailing you all a lot of fundraising asks in the past few weeks and I am so grateful you’re all still with me. We’re so close to finishing this.
[Please contribute what you can. The numbers are clear: _you make the difference._](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260716.rnaUk1&refcode=em20260717-3044&t=3&akid=3044%2E105371%2Exs7kkB)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260716.rnaUk1&amount=5&refcode=em20260717-3044&t=6&akid=3044%2E105371%2Exs7kkB)**
With gratitude,
Francesca
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260717-3044&t=7&refcode2=3044_105371_xs7kkB&akid=3044%2E105371%2Exs7kkB)**

If you joined us at the Rocky Mountain Voice Freedom Festival, thank you for helping make it such an incredible celebration of America's 250th Birthday and Colorado's 150th Birthday. If you couldn't make it, we've got you covered.
🎥 Our official _**[RMV Freedom Festival sizzle reel](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_ is now live! Relive the energy, the speakers, the music, the rodeo, and the unforgettable moments that brought thousands of Coloradans together.

[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Wildfires prompted Polis to [extend state tax deadlines](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for a dozen counties, while Xcel's rate hike draws scrutiny after [shutoffs jumped 705 percent since 2023](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) despite executives [denying an affordability crisis](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) — a claim at odds with a survey showing [85 percent cite cost of living as a top concern](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and CNBC's [worst-ever ranking for the state](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Douglas County also approved a [$22.8 million Axon camera contract](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), Polis drew fire over a [Zimbabwe socialism jab](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) at a Fort Collins legislator, and a [right-to-hunt-and-fish measure cleared](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) its signature hurdle for November.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** [DSA unveiled a platform](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to draft a new constitution, abolish the Senate and Electoral College, and subordinate the presidency and Supreme Court to Congress, as [membership hits a record 120,000](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Trump [pushed ICE to resume traffic stops](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after a brief pause following two fatal migrant shootings, and unveiled documents he says [show officials hid Chinese election hacking in 2020](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Treasury also [revealed a Trump $1 coin](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for the nation's 250th, and the House passed a bill [making daylight saving time permanent](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Writing for The Gazette, Chris Dorsey argues [gun owners could again be a decisive voting bloc](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), crediting NRA organizing for judicial appointments now driving the Court's new willingness to hear challenges to state rifle restrictions.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, July 17, 2026.
– Team RMV

**[Xcel says it has no affordability crisis. Its customers and regulatory filings tell another story.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Every week, Carlos H. sits down with his bills and works out what his family can go without.
Some weeks it is dinner. “I just opt out to say, hey, okay, maybe won’t be cooking up something tonight, so we can just make ends meet,” the Denver father said. Some weeks it is gas—a quarter tank instead of a full one, and the math of whether that gets him to the next payday. He has a 14-year-old daughter and a baby due in February.
His electric bill runs $120 to $150 a month. A proposed Xcel settlement could push it higher. “We don’t have an affordability crisis,” Robert Kenney, president of Xcel Energy Colorado, told the House Energy and Environment Committee on April 23, arguing against a proposal to give regulators more power over how utilities finance new projects.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[The rise of DSA, and a platform to rewrite the Constitution.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_With a Denver DSA member just winning a U.S. House primary and five active Colorado chapters, this isn't a fringe movement — and its platform calls for abolishing the Senate, rewriting the Constitution, and granting amnesty to all immigrants regardless of status._

* DSA's newly launched platform calls for drafting a new constitution, abolishing the Senate and Electoral College, and replacing the president and Supreme Court with branches subordinate to Congress — a measure adopted 12 to 11, with a key supporter from a caucus whose stated goal is, in its own words, "communism."

* The same platform calls for abolishing ICE, amnesty for all immigrants regardless of status, fully abolishing police and prisons, public ownership of major corporations, universal rent control, a 32-hour work week at full pay, and canceling all student debt.

* Colorado has five active DSA chapters with roughly 1,800 Denver members, a DSA-backed candidate just defeated a 30-year House incumbent in Denver's primary, and a new poll shows 47% of self-identified liberals now believe socialism is a better economic system than capitalism.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

These concerns led Denver to drop its contract with Flock, while a bill in the state legislature that would have required warrants for most searches of license plate data died in April after pushback from law enforcement._

Ashley Webb drew attention during the undercard portion of the Democratic Senate replacement debate. Webb's appearance overshadowed several better-known candidates and turned the debate into a viral moment. Additionally, Maine Wire reporter Seamus Othot, reported on a Facebook group for Hispanics in Maine that he said has become a hub for cash work, lodging, nanny services, home massage ads and other questionable offers. The group illustrates how informal labor markets can raise concerns about illegal work, exploitation, taxes and public accountability.

Why? Because he wants to distract from the failures of his administration – that he is tanking our economy and costs are going up, that he can’t figure out how to get out of this war with Iran, that he can’t even figure out how to fix the paint in the reflecting pool.

We've defeated Donald Trump's lies about our elections here in Michigan before, and we will do it again. In the State Senate, where I chair the Elections Committee, we pushed forward a state Voting Rights Act to protect your right to vote after the Supreme Court gutted the federal Voting Rights Act.

**Now I'm running for Congress to stop Donald Trump's attempts to federalize our elections and to finally pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act.

| | | | | |
Team Mackenzie,
**This is getting ridiculous. Yesterday the latest Bob Brooks scandal appeared, this time from the news outlet Townhall...**
**Bob had his wife donate the maximum allowed to his campaign – TWICE during the Primary. Here’s the problem: they used her maiden name the one time and her married name the next to circumvent campaign finance laws**. That’s pretty ironic coming from the man who says we need campaign finance reform.
**Another day. Another Bob Brooks scandal. The people of the 7th District deserve better.**
---
| [Read Story Here](https://us.list-manage.com/cCyct1LCNUK?e=5ccada9200&c2id=772b190546f65300d48df506f9534e27)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/HuTCWlKsjFd?e=5ccada9200&c2id=772b190546f65300d48df506f9534e27)
| |
"A review of Brooks' FEC filings shows a pair of suspicious donations. Last year, Brooks' campaign received a $3,500 primary individual donation from a 'Jennifer Crook' and another $3,500 primary individual donation from 'Jennifer Brooks,' with both contributions coming from the same address...
The maximum amount individuals can donate for an election cycle is $7,000; $3,500 for the primary election and an additional $3,500 for the general election. Both of these donations were made for the primary election, a violation of campaign finance laws.
Jennifer Brooks is Bob Brooks' wife, and her maiden name is Crook. On July 13, Politico reported that the Brooks campaign confirmed the donations were made by Jennifer Brooks...
**These questionable campaign donations are not a one-off incident.**
Brooks is currently involved in ongoing litigation that alleges he transferred property to his current wife to avoid having to pay his former in-laws a $130,000 debt. According to the Lehigh Valley Ramblings, a lawsuit was filed on February 17 alleging that Brooks and his current wife engaged in a 'fraudulent conveyance' to avoid a judgment owed to Brooks' former mother-in-law. In 2008, Brooks' former in-laws transferred residential property to Brooks and his first wife, including fronting the cost of subdividing the property for $55,000. Brooks and his first wife reportedly signed a promissory note for what they owed on the property but never paid. He was sued, and a judgment for $130,000 was entered against him in 2020. Brooks filed an appeal and lost in a unanimous Pennsylvania Superior Court ruling. In 2022, a judgment for $130,000 was filed against Brooks.
Brooks and his first wife divorced in 2018. Here's where things get even shadier. Brooks' first wife is named Jennifer Lynne Brooks and his current wife is named Jennifer Lynn Brooks (nee Crook). The current lawsuit against Brooks alleges he sought to obscure the identity of his second wife by using a quitclaim deed and the similar names to avoid paying the $130,000 judgment. The current lawsuit, in which the plaintiff says the signature on the original promissory note, signed by Brooks' first wife, is substantially different from the signature on the quitclaim deed. The lawsuit seeks $160,000 from Brooks and his current wife as well as punitive damages for 'outrageous and malicious subterfuge that shock the conscience.'"

The Village Creek floodplain in Birmingham will receive more than $2.6 million in federal funding secured by U.S. Sen. Katie Britt to address decades of recurring flooding.

Britt (R-Montgomery), chair of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Homeland Security, secured $2.645 million for the City of Birmingham through the Fiscal Year 2026 Homeland Security Appropriations Act.

The funding will support ongoing efforts to restore the Village Creek floodplain, reduce stormwater flowing into the creek and limit flooding in nearby communities, particularly Ensley.

“For decades, the City of Birmingham has worked to restore the Village Creek floodplain and implement a long-term solution to flooding,” Britt said.

| | Dear Peter,
[Join us TOMORROW, Saturday July 18th at 11AM PT / 2PM ET, to rally and to get out the vote for Kshama Sawant!](https://us.list-manage.com/17Y_YSj4503?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) Come out in person to Pratt Park in Seattle, or join the livestream from anywhere!
Working people and oppressed communities globally are facing an emergency situation. There is an ongoing genocide of the Palestinian people being carried out by the Israeli state in Gaza and the West Bank. There are many wars and military assaults being carried out by US imperialism, like the war on Iran and other military campaigns in the Middle East, in African countries like Somalia, and in South America. All of this is resulting in immense suffering and bloodshed for millions of people.
In the US, most Americans are struggling with the skyrocketing cost of basic necessities, like groceries, rent, and healthcare. At the same time the ultra rich in the top 1% have amassed $55 trillion in wealth.
All of this is happening because both the Democratic and Republican parties serve the interests of the billionaires, and both are warmongering parties down to their bones. We urgently need a class struggle based fight back. Right now that means electing Kshama Sawant to Congress, and to do that we need to get into the general election, which means fighting hard for every vote in the next few weeks.
Most of the time working people have no political representation under capitalism. AIPAC-backed candidates like Democrat Adam Smith, Kshama's main opponent, loudly flaunt their support for war and consistently vote in the interests of big corporations and the billionaires. Adam Smith needs to be thrown out of office, along with all the other members of Congress who have made a comfortable career for themselves by voting for war after war, and making sure the rich get richer. Smith, as a ranking member of the House Armed Services Committee, is a general among the war hawks, and has never met a war he didn't like. He has voted to send tens of billions of dollars in military funding for Israel's genocide of the Palestinian people and deadly invasion of Lebanon, and he has voted repeatedly to block UN food aid to the Palestinian people. Smith voted for the $906 billion dollar war budget that Trump has used to carry out the war on Iran. Now Smith is proposing $1.15 trillion for war and bloodshed for next year's war budget.
Working people across the country are furious at these AIPAC-backed warmongers who have been in office for decades. Several of these incumbents have been defeated in primary elections in New York and Colorado. Kshama Sawant’s independent revolutionary socialist campaign has the potential to deal the biggest blow yet to the Zionist lobby because of Kshama's demand to end all military aid to Israel combined with her unique track record of leading movements to defeat the billionaires and the political establishment over and over again.
Kshama was on the Seattle City Council for ten years and won major victories, like the nation's highest minimum wage, the Amazon Tax, and landmark renters' rights. Kshama commandeered the political agenda of the Seattle City Council time and time again, and forced the Democratic Party to concede to the demands of working people. We need this kind of shake up in the halls of Congress.
[Come out to Pratt Park on July 18th to rally with Kshama and to get out the vote.](https://us.list-manage.com/17AUJMnK5oz?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) We have only a few weeks left to get Kshama into the general election. If we are able to do this, it would be a head to head battle between AIPAC and billionaire-backed Smith, and the antiwar independent socialist who beat the billionaires, Kshama Sawant. This battle would be absolutely electrifying for people across the country, but it cannot happen without you. We need everyone to join us for the rally in person or over livestream, and please join the canvassing on the ground or phonebanking happening immediately afterwards.
Solidarity,Kshama for Congress

**Shuster here --and what a week!** The Iran war is back on, the news is heavy, and [David Shuster](https://open.substack.com/users/16891317-david-shuster?utm_source=mentions)'s antidote is the one that always works: the five sharpest pieces of AI political satire the internet coughed up this week, counted down from five to one. This edition has a rap battle, a beloved wizarding franchise recast with an all-too-familiar villain, a musical tribute no cabinet official asked for, and one senator's hotly disputed proof of life. It is the week's madness run through a comedy filter, and it is exactly what your blood pressure ordered.
We are not going to spoil the countdown--least of all the number-one slot, which Shuster only half-jokes he should reserve for this creator every single week. Five clips, four minutes, and not an ounce of mercy for the powerful. Hit play, laugh where you are supposed to, and see if you can call the order before he gets to the top. Then tell us in the comments which one you would have crowned.

body:
109 Days till Election! Can you believe it?

| | | [ ](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn11JJNENg30eeUPXVkqayxCfDLIkkjdPcC_U3XuHRoCIwMELeQenzQ2oHmoOYJU340&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=1)
---
Summer is in full swing, and our campaign is moving faster than ever! We’ve been hitting the road, showing up everywhere we can, and listening to the issues that matter most to the voters. From standing up for our local water supplies to meeting with neighbors at community town halls, the energy across TX-27 is amazing. **Thank you for being the heart of this campaign—we couldn’t do it without you.** Check out what we have coming up this week and a few highlights from this past month on the trail! **_This Upcoming Week at a Glance_** As we move into the weeks ahead, our focus remains on expanding conversations across the district and continuing to show up in every corner of TX-27. This upcoming weekend, we have a packed schedule, which means more opportunities to connect with the voters across the district! From on-the-ground events to conversations with neighbors, this month is all about building momentum and strengthening the relationships that drive this campaign forward. _Saturday_ | (9:30) **Block Walking in Lockhart** \- We would love to have you with us for an early morning of block walking as we change hearts and minds, one knock at a time! _Saturday_ | (1:00) **Data Center Protests in Victoria** \- Join us tomorrow for the AI Data[ Center National Day of Protest](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=KTUZ3zNMCUbssfVMw_qmoL3KJDFDB_7_ftFLQemw-CTF6v7tPr8thsyPJhJTXq1E&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=2) in the fight to protect our water supply. _Sunday_ | (1:00) [**KBAD Monthly Membership Meeting**](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=SfrCTE8ss2RatbuMtShZWl9GhZOLFMQqz12qNJALC78&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=3) \- Kyle and Buda are the key to turning TX27 blue. Show up and learn what we can do to flip this district. _Wednesday_ | (9:00) **Mom’s for Change Meet and Greet in Victoria** \- Join us at the Victoria Park Pavillion to learn about what is preventing women from voting and educate each other about how, where, and when to vote. _Wednesday_ | (6:30) **AI Data Center Town Hall** \- If you are local to Bastrop County, we would love to see you here. Please remember to RSVP at [LIV.org](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=1wC8lCRrPkfk40dlbqoqv94GomxPJiLYkAve_u3Rd3qeMBcteAcjI32gdZM2OU35mTMJKcOc0NlhuCVgsBpj0nn4XiqoZYUzoZnp3y9h_UUL9Qsjw4S3ZOtEHmt7i3WX&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=4), and come see what happens when Democrats, Republicans, and Independents band together to fight for our communities.
---
**_Staff Spotlight!_** We are excited to announce that the Tanya for Texas Campaign has gained some new, talented staff! Samantha "Sam" Davis has joined as Campaign Manager. Brandon Clear is our Lead Organizer. And we are so lucky to have their passion, dedication, and hard work.
---
**_June Highlights_** **Bastrop County Data Center Meeting** | I stood alongside the residents of Bastrop County as they pushed back against the expansion of data centers in their community—something we are all too familiar with across our district. We showed up to voice our concerns, ask the hard questions, and fight for our rural Texas communities. **Portland Lunch & Coastal Bend Town Hall** | I have put over 65,000 miles on my car, driving from Circle C in Austin all the way to Portland. Leading up to the Democratic Convention, I did just that again—gathering with leaders all across the Coastal Bend, I had the privilege of meeting with Democrats and hearing about the issues that matter most to them. **Happy Hour Event** | Delegates from all across TX-27 gathered for a happy hour while in Corpus Christi for the Texas Democratic Convention. I loved seeing people from across the district get to know each other and strategize on how to build infrastructure for winning in November! **Texas Democratic Convention** | On the final day of the state convention, I had the honor of taking the stage and addressing the thousands of delegates who gathered in Corpus Christi. It was a fantastic ending to a weekend full of caucuses, meet-and-greets, strategy sessions, and speeches to keep the momentum going and help turn Texas blue! _If you weren’t able to make it to the convention, you can watch it here:_[_Convention Speech_](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=gtygs8y15la-QqWnug14PF5sca1LxVdyawaUmVA2f3LlWx9G-81Fygh0RtwlI6RHd6HXkzG6JOpPI1WYk0vVHg&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=5) **_We have yard signs available!_** If you would like one and live in District 27, please fill out this [form](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/volunteer?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=6). We are making upgrades to our website. Everything you need to know before you vote: [Voter Info](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/voter_info?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=7) Please feel free to forward this newsletter to your network! And as always, thank you for being a part of this campaign. We are grateful for y'all's support!! Until next Friday. Have a great weekend, stay safe, and stay well! _P.S. Please enjoy these pictures from the campaign trail!_
**______________________** To stay updated, please check out our socials—we appreciate the follows! [Instagram](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=mGkj6P31KIkRMZhtjQusDTV7GFpUpg6VLLUuif8PWjnWOC4lSKuv8GWqaLwO5DvX&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=8) [Facebook](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=gtygs8y15la-QqWnug14POmyE7cVjhGFcY_EAyuu8aYPN63MFjBoN881CO180NQWdZbpMYdzMIJrmMZDpBHNwA&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=9) [Website](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/?e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=10) If you’d like to make a contribution, please visit: [actblue.com](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn0XlvDo1X5NteDsJeOxzSIjywkdl8c2iNfTRzSvzGQb3Lve33NPnNz8OExPjAj5OKSkzhflpUG_7fanJMwvDnQJ&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=109_days_election_newsletter&n=11). Thank you for your time and support of our grassroots campaign! -Tanya

With less than two weeks until our FEC deadline, we have to be ready for anything.
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1317?t=1&akid=904%2E3892029%2E5HaEQJ)

$5.
That’s the donation I am asking you to chip in today to help flip Florida blue and win back the Senate in November.
More than 200,000 people have joined our campaign for change so far. 200,000 people doing what they can to defeat Ashley Moody, take back the Senate, and deliver a democratic check on an out-of-control Trump administration.
But the last FEC deadline before the Primary Election is coming up fast, and we have to be ready for anything.
Donald Trump knows how important our election is too. If MAGA loses this seat, then Democrats are virtually guaranteed to take back the Senate majority. That’s why he endorsed Ashley Moody early on and has already rallied for her in Florida. It’s also why special interests are pouring money into helping her win this election.
Florida’s Senate race came down to less than 1 percentage point in the last Trump midterm election. Just a few thousand votes could decide this race. We can’t leave anything to chance, so I am humbly asking:
[**Will you please donate $5 or whatever amount you can afford to help me flip Florida and take back our Senate majority?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em260717-2&amount=5&refcode2=904_3892029_5HaEQJ&akid=904%2E3892029%2E5HaEQJ)

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

First, Justice Democrats faced a couple of hard losses in 2024, when AIPAC
successfully ousted Squad members Cori Bush and Jamaal Bowman from
Congress after the two leaders fought to end the genocide in Gaza.

Then, in April last year, Axios reported that “House Democrats' headaches
are about to get much worse” and predicted this year’s many primary
fights, quoting our Communications Director Usamah Andrabi:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260717-2.PFbpQM&refcode=em20260717-38045&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38045%2E1203867%2EJR0jcT ]Screenshot from Axios: Usamah Andrabi, a spokesperson for Justice
Democrats, told Axios the number of House Democrats who ultimately draw
serious challengers “could be dozens — it could be a large portion of the
caucus.”

Now, one year later, we’re nearing the end of the 2026 election cycle with
8 primary victories — and we’re not finished yet.

After endorsing 15 primary candidates challenging out-of-touch Democratic
incumbents or running for open seats, we’re sending at least 6 new Justice
Democrats to Congress, with 2 additional candidates advancing to the
general, and 3 more primaries to go.

When all is said and done, we could see almost a dozen progressives join
our existing bloc in Congress, doubling our power in a single cycle!

That’s what happens when regular people in working-class communities
across the country come together and fight back against the billionaires,
super PACs, and corporate lobby groups. Organized people can beat
organized money.

What we’re seeing this year isn’t limited to a single moment or candidate:
this is what a people-powered movement that’s fed up with the status quo
looks like, and we’re not going anywhere.
